articles.title: Batería baja y sobrecalentamiento: señales de que te espían por la cámara del celular
articles.text:
Una batería que se descarga rápido, un teléfono que se calienta sin una causa evidente o un consumo de datos fuera de lo habitual pueden advertir sobre problemas de seguridad, como el spyware, un virus que accede a la cámara del celular, ve la pantalla y extrae información sin que el usuario lo advierta.
El spyware puede afectar el rendimiento porque ocupa memoria, procesador y batería. Entre las consecuencias figuran cierres inesperados de aplicaciones, demoras al abrir funciones y bloqueos momentáneos.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, los expertos señalan que estos indicios no confirman por sí solos una intrusión. El desgaste de la batería puede responder a aplicaciones exigentes, actualizaciones o fallas del celular. Aun así, cuando varias señales aparecen al mismo tiempo, conviene revisar permisos, aplicaciones instaladas y actividad del dispositivo.
Por qué la cámara del celular se activa sola o deja de estar disponible
Según ESET, una de las alertas más visibles aparece cuando la cámara se abre sin que nadie la haya activado. En algunos teléfonos, un indicador luminoso informa que una aplicación usa la cámara o el micrófono. Si esa señal se enciende sin motivo conocido, corresponde identificar qué programa tiene acceso a esos componentes.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, puede ocurrir lo contrario: al intentar abrir la cámara, el sistema informa que otra aplicación ya utiliza esa función. Ese mensaje no prueba una infección, porque puede ser por una videollamada o a una aplicación abierta en segundo plano.
Sin embargo, si se repite y no hay una explicación clara, es clave cerrar las apps activas y controlar los permisos concedidos.
Qué sucede si aparecen fotos que no tomó el usuario del teléfono
La presencia de fotos o videos desconocidos en la galería merece una revisión inmediata. Un archivo que no corresponde a una captura realizada por el propietario puede indicar que una aplicación accedió a la cámara, aunque existen explicaciones menos graves, como imágenes descargadas desde mensajería o copias automáticas desde otros dispositivos vinculados.
PUBLICIDAD
El primer paso consiste en verificar la fecha, la hora y la carpeta de origen del archivo. Si el contenido fue creado desde la cámara del teléfono y no hay registro de que alguien lo haya tomado, se aconseja analizar las aplicaciones que poseen ese permiso.
Para prevenir riesgos y robos, ESET sugiere retirar el acceso a la cámara y al micrófono de los programas que no lo necesitan para funcionar.
Por qué la batería se descarga rápido y el dispositivo se sobrecalienta
La descarga acelerada de la batería y el sobrecalentamiento figuran entre las señales que pueden asociarse con programas espía. Un software que permanece activo de manera oculta, registra información o transmite archivos consume recursos incluso cuando el teléfono parece estar en reposo.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, estos síntomas pueden estar vinculados con una batería degradada, juegos, transmisión de video, mala cobertura de red o temperaturas ambientales elevadas.
La clave está en observar si el consumo se produjo de forma repentina y si coincide con aplicaciones desconocidas, actividad de la cámara o uso de datos que no se puede explicar.
Qué pasa si el consumo de datos aumentó sin explicación
Quien controla de forma remota una cámara necesita transferir las imágenes o videos obtenidos. Por eso, un incremento inesperado en el uso de datos puede ser otra señal de alerta. La revisión debe incluir tanto el consumo general como el detalle por aplicación que ofrecen Android e iOS.
PUBLICIDAD
Una app con un gasto elevado de datos sin una función que lo justifique requiere atención. El problema puede agravarse si la actividad ocurre cuando el celular permanece bloqueado o conectado a una red WiFi.
Por este motivo, revisar el historial de consumo permite detectar programas que envían información en segundo plano y limitar su acceso a internet si fuera necesario.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Testing two Thunderbolt 5 docks with M.2 storage — VectoTech V-Core vs Orico TB5
articles.text:
Testing two Thunderbolt 5 docks with M.2 storage — VectoTech V-Core vs Orico TB5
Both include 2.5 GbE LAN and internal M.2 slots, but the cheaper makes too many design and feature sacrifices.
The Thunderbolt 5 market is starting to heat up, as we’re seeing more players enter the increasingly crowded field. We’ve previously looked at docks in the sub-$400 price category, and premium offerings crossing the $600 barrier.
Today, we’re focusing on two new entries in the sub-$400 category: the VectoTech V-Core and the Orico TB5, priced at $349 and $399, respectively. Both offer a wealth of USB and Thunderbolt ports, 2.5 GbE Ethernet, and internal M.2 slots. While their specs look similar on paper, at the end of our testing, there was a clear winner.
VectoTech V-Core
Design of the VectoTech V-Core Thunderbolt 5 Dock
The V-Core has what I’d call a traditional, candybar form factor. It’s meant to sit flat on your desk, unlike chunkier docks that can also operate vertically. At first glance, I thought the V-Core was made of lightweight aluminum. However, it wasn’t until I started fumbling around, trying to figure out how to access the internal M.2 SSD slot, that I discovered the unfortunate truth: the V-Core is constructed almost entirely of plastic. That includes the lower and top chassis, and much of the internal structure.
It’s a stark departure from every other Thunderbolt dock that I’ve tested, which are made from aluminum to help dissipate heat – which can be intense when a dock is under load. In addition, the top cover wiggled around when snapped into place (it uses a friction fit to attach to the main chassis).
With the top cover removed, you can see an internal cooling fan, which is essential for cooling Thunderbolt 5 docks with internal SSD bays, and a large black aluminum heatsink held in place with two screws. After removing the screws, the heatsink lifts off, revealing an M.2 slot that supports up to an 8TB 2280 SSD. Here’s another nitpick: Instead of using a screw to secure the SSD, VectoTech uses a tiny, spinning plastic retaining clip.
This is a feature that’s handy to have on motherboards when you’re often reaching inside a case, sometimes while the case is vertical. But it makes less sense in a small dock – especially when this particular latch is smaller than we’ve seen on other M.2 mounts. It didn’t inspire much confidence that it would hold the SSD in place, at least not compared to traditional screws. That said, VectoTech offers thermal pads that cover both the top and bottom of your SSD.
When it comes to ports, the VectoTech V-Core left me scratching my head a bit: There are no native HDMI or DisplayPort ports on the dock. Most Thunderbolt docks include at least one of the two common video ports, so it was disappointing to see this omission here. It’s not the end of the world, however; you can always use an HDMI-to-USB-C or DisplayPort-to-USB-C adapter with the dock (at an additional out-of-pocket cost).
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Front
- 1x Thunderbolt 5 upstream (80 Gbps bi-directional, 140W)
- 1x Thunderbolt 5 downstream (80 Gbps bi-directional, 60W)
- 1x USB-A 3.2 Gen 2
- 1x SD UHS-II slot
- 1x audio combo jack
Back
- 2x Thunderbolt 5 downstream (80 Gbps bi-directional, 15W)
- 2x USB-A 3.2 Gen 2
- 1x USB-A 3.2 Gen 1
- 1x 2.5 GbE (RJ45) port
- 1x 240W power port
Instead, you’ll find two Thunderbolt 5 ports on the front (one upstream, one downstream), a USB-A port, an SD 4.0 reader (no microSD), and a 3.5 mm headphone jack. Moving to the back, there are three additional USB-A ports, two downstream Thunderbolt 5 ports, and a 2.5 GbE port.
Orico TB5
Design of the Orico TB5 Thunderbolt 5 Desktop Workstation
Unlike the V-Core, the Orico TB5 has a chassis primarily constructed of a single piece of thick aluminum. The outer chassis has an oblong shape, with ventilation cutouts on the right and left sides.
The front and rear fascias are plastic, and where you’ll find the assortment of ports.
Front
- 3x USB-A 3.2 Gen 2
- 1x Thunderbolt 5 downstream (80 Gbps bi-directional, 60W)
- 1x SD UHS-II slot
- 1x microSD UHS-II slot
- 1x audio combo jack
Back
- 1x Thunderbolt 5 upstream (80 Gbps bi-directional, 140W)
- 1x Thunderbolt 5 downstream (80 Gbps bi-directional, 60W)
- 1x HDMI
- 1x DisplayPort
- 1x 2.5 GbE (RJ45) port
- 1x 240W power port
Up front, you’ll find an SD 4.0 slot, a microSD 4.0 slot, three USB-A ports (10 Gbps), one USB-C port (also 10 Gbps), and one Thunderbolt 5 downstream port. On the back, there’s one Thunderbolt 5 upstream port, one Thunderbolt 5 downstream port, one USB-C port, one DisplayPort, one HDMI port, a 2.5 GbE port, and a 3.5mm audio combo jack.
I was somewhat surprised to see both HDMI and DisplayPort in this relatively compact Thunderbolt 5 dock, but they are welcome additions here. It’s hard to be disappointed with Orico’s choice of ports on the TB5, as there’s a nice balance of USB-A, USB-C, and video outputs.
But my absolute favorite design feature of the TB5 is on its underside. Most Thunderbolt docks that feature an internal SSD slot require you to remove a screw to access the M.2 slot. However, the TB5 uses a magnetic cover that is easily removed with a fingernail, yet strong enough to remain attached when moving the dock around. It’s a small touch, but appreciated when swapping SSDs. The M.2 slot can accommodate 2280 form-factor SSDs.
Testing
Testing the VectoTech V-Core and Orico TB5 Thunderbolt 5 Docks
The lack of native DisplayPort and HDMI ports didn’t hamper my testing with the V-Core. My primary desktop rig uses a 49-inch WQHD monitor with native USB-C support, and it connected to the V-Core without issue at its native 240 Hz refresh rate with a Windows 11 PC and a Mac running macOS 27. I also tested the same monitor using the HDMI-to-USB-C and DisplayPort-to-USB-C adapters that I have on hand. Again, I had no issues with this setup.
The dock itself did get very hot; just as hot as the many aluminum-shelled Thunderbolt 5 docks I’ve tested. Although I didn’t experience any slowdowns or errors after extended use, I do wonder about heat soak with the plastic enclosure over time. The internal fan definitely helps, but it’s a concern that lingers at the back of my mind.
I tested the Orico TB5 across USB-C, DisplayPort, and HDMI connections without any performance issues or hiccups. Like the V-Core, the TB5 also includes an internal cooling fan.
Everything that I threw at both docks worked without issue. I hooked up USB mice and keyboards, my iPhone Air, a 1TB USB-C thumb drive, an Orico Thunderbolt 5 SSD dock, multiple portable USB-C monitors, and a DJI Mini 5 Pro drone. I also tested the 2.5 GbE LAN on both docks on my TP-Link Deco BE63 home network.
Among recent Thunderbolt 5 docks we've tested, the V-Core was at the back of the pack in both sequential read and write speeds (5,371.96 MBps and 4,083.95 MBps, respectively). Orico’s TB5, on the other hand, landed in second place, behind the UGREEN Revodock MaxiDok in sequential reads (5,745.11 MBps), and led the pack in sequential writes (4,335.56 MBps).
When testing the 2.5 GbE LAN on both docks, both maxed out at around 2,300 Mbps using iPerf3, which is right in line with what we would expect after taking into account TCP/IP packet overhead.
Bottom Line
Bottom Line
The VectoTech V-Core and the Orico TB5 are similarly priced and feature a similar form factor, but Orico’s TB5 is by far the superior entry here. For starters, it just feels like a more premium product, with its aluminum enclosure versus the V-Core's plastic. And accessing the internal M.2 slot on the TB5 is much easier, requiring a simple tug on the magnetic access door, versus prying off the plastic cover on the V-Core, removing two screws, and then prying off the internal heatsink.
In other ways that matter to most people, the TB5 includes native DisplayPort and HDMI connections for your monitors. The V-Core is USB only (necessitating a USB-C adapter for most monitors). And finally, while the V-Core was at the back of the pack in storage performance compared to its peers, the TB5 trended near the front.
Right now, the VectoTech V-Core is priced at $349 on Amazon, versus $399 for the Orico TB5. A $50 premium is certainly enough to consider going with the cheaper option. But more and better ports, faster throughput, and a better, more premium design make the Orico worth paying extra for.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: Which Audio-to-Text Tool Works Best for Client Briefings? Converting a Conversation Into a Brief That Drives Action - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Client briefings almost never follow a single pattern. Some take place on a scheduled video call, some happen face to face, and some show up later as a voice memo.
What stays consistent is the outcome teams need: not a verbatim transcript, but an actionable brief that captures the objective, requirements, decisions, non-negotiables, and who is responsible for what next. Notta aligns well with that goal because it supports all three capture scenarios within one product and, unlike tools centered on a single capture approach, includes a local processing option for briefings that should not leave the device.
Capture Method Is Not the Same Thing as Confidentiality
A few labels get used interchangeably in this space, but they are not equivalent, particularly when a briefing involves pricing, strategy, or other sensitive details.
- Live bot capture. A visible participant joins the meeting to record and transcribe. Fireflies and Notta both support this and both also provide a bot-free alternative, so a bot is optional rather than mandatory.
- Bot-free capture. No bot joins the meeting; the device captures audio. That still does not guarantee on-device processing. Granola is bot-free yet routes captured audio to cloud transcription and AI providers, similar to Notta’s Bot-Free mode and Fireflies’ Desktop App.
- Local, offline processing. Recording and transcription are handled on the device, without sending content to a vendor cloud. In this comparison, Notta Desktop Privacy Mode is the only example, and its availability varies by plan, operating system, installed model, and language.
- Upload-first transcription. A recording is uploaded after the fact for transcription. Sonix and Descript are built around this workflow, and Notta also supports it through file upload. This is separate from local processing.
Bot-free can be a meaningful requirement for client briefings, but it is not the same as local processing, and only one tool here offers both. A note on consent: bot-free capture does not remove consent obligations. Applicable law, client policy, and platform requirements still need to be followed before recording, and recording should be disclosed. This is not legal advice.
Comparison Table
1. Notta
Best For: Consultants, agencies and client-facing teams whose briefings span virtual calls, in-person meetings and existing recordings, and who occasionally need one to stay off the cloud.
A video call is only one form a client briefing can take. Notta handles that scenario with a bot on supported platforms and, when a bot is not appropriate, Bot-Free capture via Notta Desktop that records system audio and microphone input without adding a visible attendee. That bot-free path still uploads audio encrypted for cloud transcription, so it addresses call visibility rather than strict confidentiality. The other common briefing formats are covered as well: in-person conversations can be captured using Notta Memo, a pocket-sized recorder, along with the mobile and Apple Watch apps; previously recorded briefings can be handled through file upload. Notta Brain can then draft a more complete brief using a template and can reference earlier meetings with the same client, surfacing a requirement raised previously but not repeated in the current discussion. It can also turn the outcome into the follow-up itself: when Gmail is connected, it saves a new draft or a reply draft in Gmail for review and sending, rather than sending anything automatically. For teams working in Slack, @Notta mentions can be used to ask questions or initiate tasks, share Brain’s answers, sources, files and generated outputs into a chosen channel, and receive results from scheduled tasks there automatically.
Privacy Mode goes beyond bot-free capture by using an installed offline model to transcribe directly on the device, and it is something teams should verify rather than assume. It requires a Pro, Business or Enterprise plan, is available only in Notta Desktop, needs an offline model installed locally, and supports English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese and Cantonese, extending to eleven languages via Apple Speech Analyzer on macOS 26 and later. It applies at the app level rather than per recording, and when enabled it pauses or limits cloud transcription, cloud AI summaries, cross-device sync and team collaboration.
Features:
- Bot, Bot-Free desktop capture, Privacy Mode, Notta Memo, mobile and Apple Watch recording, file and link upload
- Notta Brain summaries, action items, brief drafting and cross-meeting recall, exporting to TXT, DOCX, XLSX, PDF, SRT and VTT
- Follow-up email drafts saved into Gmail for review when Gmail is connected, never sent automatically
- Slack access through @Notta mentions, channel sharing of answers, sources, files and outputs, and automatic delivery of scheduled task results
- CRM sync to seven platforms on Business and above: Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, Zendesk Sell, Freshsales and Salesflare
Pros:
- Handles virtual, in-person and previously recorded briefings within one product
- The only tool in this set with a supported local, offline mode rather than only a bot-free approach
- Notta Brain can reference a client’s prior briefings, not only the latest meeting
- Follow-up work exits as a Gmail draft or a Slack update, keeping post-briefing admin in the tools teams already use
Cons:
- Privacy Mode depends on plan, operating system, installed model and language, and pauses cloud AI summaries and sync while active
- Standard Bot-Free recording is not local processing; audio still reaches Notta’s cloud
- Free limits of 120 minutes a month and 3 minutes per conversation are tight for regular briefings
2. Granola
Granola positions itself around invisibility on calls. Instead of joining as a meeting bot, it captures system audio on the device and combines that capture with notes the user types, using those bullets to shape what the AI elaborates on. That said, it does not perform local transcription: Granola’s security page identifies transcription providers such as Deepgram and AssemblyAI and AI providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, so “bot-free” in this context means no visible attendee, not that data stays off third-party servers. Granola’s documentation also states it is not currently HIPAA compliant and should not be used for protected health information, with compliance targeted by end of 2026.
Features:
- Bot-free capture on Mac and Windows, with iOS, Android and Apple Watch apps for in-person briefings
- Notion, HubSpot, Slack, Zapier, Attio and Affinity integrations, plus MCP and API access, on Business
Pros:
- No visible bot at all, including no bot option, which some clients prefer
- The mix of typed notes plus transcript can yield a more relevant brief than a purely automated summary
- Flat $14 per user per month on Business, with no annual commitment for the price
Cons:
- Bot-free capture is not local processing; audio still reaches third-party cloud providers
- Not HIPAA compliant by its own documentation, and model training is opt-out for standard users, off by default only on Enterprise
- No option to join as a bot when a client would actually prefer a visible notetaker
3. Fireflies
Fireflies stands out for how widely it connects across the stack. It can capture meetings with a bot on Zoom, Meet, Teams and Webex, and it also offers bot-free capture through its Desktop App on Windows 10+ and macOS 12+, plus capture via a Chrome extension, mobile app and web recorder. AskFred can answer questions about a single briefing or across multiple meetings, transcription supports 100+ languages, and the integration catalog reaches 100+ apps including thirteen CRM platforms.
For client briefings, the trade-offs show up in the same areas this comparison emphasizes. Every capture method sends audio to Fireflies’ cloud, including botless capture, so it does not provide a local option for briefings that must remain on-device. In-person capture is handled through the mobile app or web recorder rather than dedicated hardware, and the output is more summary-oriented, which often leaves a separate step to convert notes into a client-ready brief.
Features:
- AskFred for querying a single meeting or across many, plus AI Skills templates including BANT and MEDDIC
- 100+ integrations and thirteen CRM platforms, including Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, Close, Copper and Freshsales
Pros:
- Broadest integration and CRM ecosystem of the tools compared here
- AskFred’s cross-meeting recall retrieves a past detail without scrolling a transcript
- Transcription in 100+ languages, the widest raw coverage here
Cons:
- No documented local or on-device processing; botless capture still uploads audio to Fireflies’ cloud
- In-person capture depends on the mobile app or web recorder, with no dedicated recorder or wearable
- Transcription, notes, recap emails and template summaries consume no credits, but advanced AI draws on plan credits that are one-time on signup, pooled and not scaled by seats, with auto-subscription to the next tier unless switched off
- The Free plan’s 400 minutes of storage is team-wide, not per seat
- HIPAA compliance is Enterprise only, and the client-ready brief is still a manual rewrite
4. Descript
Descript is strongest when the goal is to turn a briefing into a polished, edited media deliverable rather than a written brief. It does not operate as a meeting bot; instead, it imports an existing Zoom cloud recording or uses its own Rooms recorder, which captures double-ended per-participant tracks and progressively uploads them during the session, helping protect the recording if a connection drops mid-briefing. Rooms is included with every plan and counts against the plan’s media minutes. Descript’s transcript-driven editing workflow can remove filler words, rearrange sections, and produce a shareable clip, which is a distinct outcome compared with the other options in this list.
Features:
- Zoom cloud recording import with multitrack transcription and speaker detection
- Transcript-based editing, including filler-word removal from Hobbyist upward
Pros:
- Produces an editable audio or video deliverable, not just a text summary
- Multitrack recording keeps each speaker separate across several stakeholders
- Progressive upload protects against a dropped connection mid-briefing
Cons:
- Not built to capture a briefing live the way a bot or bot-free desktop app is
- Editing-first workflow is more setup than most briefings need
- Transcription covers 26 languages but only one per file, so mixed-language briefings need splitting
- The free plan’s 60 media minutes a month will not cover a regular schedule
5. Sonix
Sonix is not designed to sit in a meeting as it happens. It is an upload-first platform: the briefing is captured using whatever recording setup already exists, then Sonix processes it for transcription, translation and editing afterward, with automatic imports of cloud recordings from Zoom, Teams, Meet, Webex, Drive and Dropbox. Its standout capability for client briefing workflows is redaction when the resulting brief or transcript needs to travel beyond the initial call. Segments can be flagged, reviewed, and then applied so the text appears as [REDACTED] while the audio is muted, with timecodes preserved. Redaction is available on Enterprise plans.
Features:
- Upload and auto-import transcription in 54+ languages, with translation in 55+
- SOC 2 Type II on all plans, with HIPAA compliance, a signed BAA and redaction on Enterprise
Pros:
- Strong fit for briefings involving multiple languages or a specific compliance bar
- Redaction helps when a brief circulates beyond the original call
- Pay as you go at $10 an hour suits occasional use with no subscription
Cons:
- No live capture; the briefing has to be recorded elsewhere first
- Hour-capped subscriptions add up for frequent briefings, with extra hours at $10
- Built around transcription and translation rather than structured brief drafting
6. Fathom
Fathom provides a real choice between bot and bot-free capture within the same app, with bot-free currently in beta and limited to Mac. As with Notta’s standard Bot-Free approach, neither mode is local processing, so audio is still uploaded to Fathom’s cloud. For teams focused primarily on capture, its Free plan is unusually generous: unlimited recordings, transcription and storage plus instant AI summaries. More advanced summary capabilities begin at Premium, and account-wide Ask Fathom is a beta with limited lookback on team calls. CRM behavior also needs careful reading: basic sync is capped at three users per domain, while field sync, Deal View and coaching metrics require Business.
Features:
- Unlimited recordings, transcription and storage on all plans including Free
- Basic CRM sync capped at 3 users per domain; field sync, Deal View and AI scorecards on Business
Pros:
- Bot-free capture even on the Free plan, which is rare
- Strongest free tier here for unlimited recording and storage
- Field-level CRM sync on a qualifying plan goes beyond a basic notes push
Cons:
- Bot-free capture is a Mac-only beta, not a mature cross-platform option
- No local or offline processing; both modes upload audio to Fathom’s cloud
- The three users per domain cap on basic CRM sync constrains team rollout
What to Look for in an Audio-to-Text Tool for Client Briefings
Capture flexibility. Briefings happen on video calls, in person and as existing recordings, and a tool covering only one forces a workaround for the rest.
Confidentiality, not just visibility. Keeping an extra participant off the call is a different guarantee from keeping audio off a vendor’s cloud, and sensitive briefings may need the stronger one.
Structured output over a raw transcript. Look for decisions, requirements and action items rather than searchable text.
Cross-briefing memory. Requirements from an earlier briefing are often relevant to the current one.
Multilingual accuracy, including whether mixed-language conversations are supported at all.
Cost structure that matches briefing volume. Per-seat subscriptions, credit-metered AI and pay-per-hour transcription suit different volumes.
Teams whose briefings routinely span all three formats benefit most from a tool that covers all three, which is where Notta is particularly well positioned, especially when a Privacy Mode level of assurance is required.
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need a bot-free tool for client briefings specifically?
Not always, but it reduces friction. Some clients accept a visible AI notetaker; others find it distracting or disallowed by policy. Having a bot-free option avoids renegotiating the setup meeting by meeting, and most tools listed here now provide one.
Is bot-free capture the same as private or confidential capture?
No. Bot-free simply means no additional participant joins the call. Audio can still be uploaded to a vendor cloud for transcription and AI processing, which is how Granola, Fathom’s bot-free mode, Fireflies’ Desktop App and Notta’s Bot-Free mode all work. Only a local, offline mode such as Notta’s Privacy Mode, on supported plans, platforms, models and languages, keeps audio off the cloud.
What’s the difference between a transcript and a brief?
A transcript is a record of what was said. A brief is a structured account of what was decided and what matters next: the objective, requirements, decisions and next steps, organized so someone who missed the meeting can still act. Most tools here can produce transcripts; fewer can reliably turn a briefing into a brief without manual rewriting.
Closing Take: Choosing an Audio-to-Text Tool for Real-World Briefings
For a single predictable kind of briefing, a tool built around one capture method can be enough: Fireflies when integration coverage is the priority and cloud processing is acceptable, Granola when bot-free virtual calls are the main requirement, Sonix or Descript when the briefing is already recorded and needs to become a clean transcript or an edited deliverable.
In practice, client briefings do not stay that tidy. They happen on calls, in person, and sometimes arrive as a recording captured by someone else. Notta supports that reality within one product across all three capture methods and adds Privacy Mode, a local option none of the other tools in this comparison match. With Notta Brain drafting a structured brief and recalling prior meetings instead of starting from a blank transcript each time, it remains the most complete fit for teams whose briefings are varied in format and sensitivity.

articles.title: SpaceX : revivez le tout premier vol orbital de Starship à travers des images spectaculaires
articles.text:
Après treize vols suborbitaux, Starship a enfin atteint l’orbite. Une première historique pour SpaceX, qui a pourtant bien failli y renoncer en plein vol.
Atteindre l’orbite est la condition pour déployer la nouvelle génération de satellites Starlink, puis pour emmener des astronautes vers la Lune dans le cadre du programme Artemis de la NASA.
Le 14e vol devait donc franchir un cap déterminant pour SpaceX. Starship, du haut de ses 124 mètres, a ainsi décollé ce lundi 28 septembre à 14h48 (heure de Paris) depuis Starbase, au Texas, avec 26 satellites Starlink V3 à bord. Si le vol fut une réussite, tout ne s’est pas passé sans accroc.
Du décollage à l’orbite, un vol à suspense
Tout a commencé comme prévu. Les 33 moteurs Raptor du Super Heavy, le premier étage, se sont allumés et ont arraché la fusée du sol. Si l’un d’entre eux s’est éteint pendant la montée, cela n’a pas eu de conséquence, assure SpaceX. Quelques minutes plus tard, les deux étages se sont séparés, et le booster a alors fait demi-tour et rallumé 31 de ses moteurs pour revenir vers la côte.
SpaceX en a profité pour tester ses limites en vidant volontairement son réservoir d’oxygène. Environ sept minutes après le décollage, il a amerri dans le golfe du Mexique, puis a explosé suite à une manœuvre volontaire visant à tester son système d’autodestruction.
L’étage supérieur, lui, a poursuivi son ascension, mais l’un de ses six moteurs s’est arrêté trop tôt. Les cinq autres ont donc dû pousser plus longtemps pour compenser. En direct, le commentateur de SpaceX, Dan Huot, annonce que la tentative de rejoindre l’orbite est reportée. Puis l’entreprise s’est ravisée : les équipes ont d’abord vérifié que les trois moteurs indispensables au retour fonctionnaient, et ont finalement donné leur feu vert. Un seul moteur s’est rallumé pendant 19 secondes, juste assez pour atteindre la vitesse nécessaire. Starship s’est enfin placé en orbite à environ 276 kilomètres d’altitude pour la toute première fois.
Une mission écourtée
Une fois en orbite, Starship a déployé les 26 satellites un par un pendant une trentaine de minutes. SpaceX a ensuite réussi à établir le contact avec chacun d’eux. Trop imposants pour tenir dans une fusée Falcon 9, ces satellites offrent dix fois plus de capacités que les modèles précédents, et fourniront des débits bien plus élevés aux utilisateurs. Trois d’entre eux, équipés de caméras, ont filmé le vaisseau pour permettre aux ingénieurs d’étudier l’état de son bouclier thermique.
Si le plan prévoyait six tours de la Terre et près de dix heures de mission, SpaceX a pris la décision de l’écourter par précaution. Après 3 tours, la mégafusée a rallumé un moteur pour ralentir et quitter l’orbite, une manœuvre qu’elle n’avait encore jamais réalisée. Elle a ensuite plongé dans l’atmosphère, où son bouclier a encaissé des températures de l’ordre de 1 430 ° Celsius.
Un peu plus de trois heures après le décollage, Starship a atteint le Pacifique Nord, au large d’Hawaï dans une zone de repli prévue à l’avance. Le premier étage s’est redressé, a rallumé trois moteurs et touché l’eau pile sur la cible. Il a ensuite basculé et explosé, comme c’était prévu, explique SpaceX. La FAA, l’autorité américaine de l’aviation, n’exige aucune enquête malgré quelques rebondissements, et un nouveau vol pourrait avoir lieu dès octobre. Prochaine étape probable : l’impressionnante récupération de la fusée directement avec les bras de la tour de lancement.

articles.title: Microsoft 365: Optionales Update deinstalliert Programme, statt alte zu aktualisieren
articles.text:
Microsoft 365: Optionales Update deinstalliert Programme, statt alte zu aktualisieren
Bei Updates für Microsoft-Produkte wie Windows kommt es immer wieder einmal zu Problemen. Für Aufsehen sorgte etwa der sogenannte Patch Tuesday vom 13. Januar 2026. Statt wie geplant kritische Sicherheitslücken zu schließen, brachte das Update selbst zusätzliche Probleme mit. Microsoft musste mit Notfall-Updates gegensteuern.
Lizenzen aufgehoben, Programme deinstalliert
Jetzt steht Microsoft 365 im Mittelpunkt eines Update-Problems. Mit dem optionalen Update KB5002907 für den Microsoft-Dienst sollten eigentlich Microsoft-365-Apps aktualisiert werden, die mehr als 90 Tage veraltet waren oder nicht mehr ordnungsgemäß aktualisiert wurden. Stattdessen sollen bestehende Lizenzen aufgehoben worden sein, wie Golem berichtet. Zum Teil verschwanden die betreffenden Programme auch einfach.
Der Konzern musste daher einmal mehr nachjustieren. Aufgrund von „unerwarteten Ergebnissen auf einigen Geräten“ habe Microsoft die Verteilung des Updates vorübergehend gestoppt, wie es in einer Mitteilung heißt. Betroffen sollen Computer sein, auf denen Office 2016 und Office 2019 läuft.
Microsoft 365: Update als Reparaturaktion
Das als „Reparaturaktion“ bezeichnete Update sollte laut Microsoft neben der Aktualisierungsoption den Wechsel zu einem aktuellen Build der Microsoft-365-Apps ermöglichen.
Gestartet hatte Microsoft die Verteilung des Updates Ende September 2026. Es stand für Geräte mit Windows 11, Windows 10, Windows Server 2025, Windows Server 2022 und Windows Server 2019 bereit. Es galt für Geräte, die den aktuellen Kanal oder den monatlichen Enterprise-Kanal verwenden. Weil es sich um ein optionales Update handelte, gab es aber keine automatische Installation.
Produkt erneut aktivieren oder neu installieren
Microsoft rät betroffenen Nutzer:innen jetzt, das Produkt erneut zu aktivieren beziehungsweise neu zu installieren. Sollte das nicht funktionieren, bittet Microsoft darum, den Support zu kontaktieren. Ob und wann Microsoft ein repariertes Update bereitstellt, ist nicht bekannt.

articles.title: Canadians spend 80 hours per year deciding what to watch: Roku
articles.text:
A new report from Roku has revealed new data on Canadians’ streaming habits.
In its seventh annual VOD Evolution Study, the streaming company found that Canadians spend a total of about 80 hours per year figuring out what to watch. A key reason for this, the study found, is that 59 per cent of people who stream TV said it’s hard to find something to watch because there are so many streaming services on the market. (On average, Canadians use four different streaming services, per Roku.)
Further, 60 per cent of people said they sometimes forget where to even stream a given movie or TV series. All of this comes as roughly 27 million Canadians now stream TV, a 35 per cent increase from five years ago, per Roku.
To address these kinds of issues, 65 per cent of respondents said they think ads would help them find a movie or TV show. On top of that, more than two-thirds of Canadians said they like ads to remind them when a movie or TV show they want to watch is available to stream. Thirty-five per cent of people also said that a TV home screen ad would feel less intrusive than traditional TV commercials.
According to Roku, 67 per cent of Canadians who stream take measurable action after seeing TV ads; 31 per cent search
for more info, 28 per cent visit a brand’s website, 19 per cent map look up the brand in-store, and 15 per cent scan a TV QR code.
Of course, Roku wants to promote its own curation tools here as a platform that features many streaming services within it. Some of these include free ad-supported television (FAST), which Roku notes is an option that continues to grow in popularity. Per the latest VOD Evolution Study, 84 per cent of Canadians watch ad-supported TV monthly with an average of 13 hours per week spent on these platforms, or about half of their total TV viewing.
To conduct this latest VOD Evolution Study on Roku’s behalf, Fuse Insights surveyed 2,043 Canadian adults in English and French in June 2026.

articles.title: „Jede Sprengung schafft eine neue Welt“: Wie der längste Straßentunnel der Welt unter der Nordsee entsteht
articles.text:
390 Meter unter den Fjorden: Wie Norwegen den Rogfast-Tunnel aus dem Fels sprengt
Es ist kalt, es ist sehr, sehr laut, und – wenn ich ganz ehrlich sein darf – ich fühle mich alles andere als entspannt. Außerdem ist meine Schutzbrille beschlagen.
Ich befinde mich etwa 300 Meter unter der Nordsee, in einer dunklen, feuchten Höhle. Es riecht seltsam. Und mir wird immer bewusster, wie viel Druck Millionen Tonnen Meerwasser direkt über meinem Kopf ausüben. Sie üben eine Kraft von mehr als 35 Kilogramm pro Quadratzentimeter aus – wie ein Nashornbaby, das auf einer Briefmarke steht. Nur dank großartiger Ingenieurskunst werde ich nicht zerquetscht, ertrinke oder verschwinde einfach.
Dieser Text ist in der Ausgabe 7/2026 von MIT Technology Review erschienen. Darin beschäftigen wir uns damit, wie KI die IT-Sicherheit auf den Kopf stellt. Das Heft ist in unserem Online-Shop bestellbar und im Zeitschriftenhandel erhältlich.
Ein paar hundert Meter entfernt trifft jemand Vorbereitungen, um eine riesige Felswand zu sprengen. Zum Glück habe ich eine Sicherheitseinweisung erhalten und trage einen Spezialhelm. „Keine Sorge – falls du es nicht schaffst, lassen wir deine Sachen an dein Büro zurückschicken“, sagt die Geologin Anne-Merete Gilje mit ernster Miene. Norwegischer Humor.
    
Wie ein Straßentunnel unter Norwegens berühmten Fjord entsteht
Ich bin hier, unter den berühmten Fjorden Norwegens, um mir anzusehen, wie der bald längste und tiefste Unterwasser-Straßentunnel der Welt entsteht: Rogfast (kurz für „Rogaland Fixed Link“). Ich möchte verstehen, wie man eine 26,7 Kilometer lange Autobahn baut, die an ihrer tiefsten Stelle 390 Meter unter dem Meeresspiegel verläuft.
Norwegen hat in den letzten Jahrzehnten mehr als tausend Kilometer Tunnel gebaut. Die spektakuläre Lage des Landes macht solche Bauvorhaben notwendig; zwar sind die Norweger stolz auf ihre nach Kanada zweitlängste Küstenlinie der Welt, doch um die Westküste hinauf- und hinunterzukommen, sind entweder mehrere Fährfahrten zwischen den Inseln oder große Umwege erforderlich.
    „Wir können kein Buch kaufen, um nachzulesen, wie man das macht.“
Wenn er fertig ist, soll Rogfast zwei Fährverbindungen überflüssig machen und die fünfstündige Fahrt zwischen den südwestlichen Städten Stavanger und Bergen um 40 Minuten verkürzen. Vier Fahrspuren und zwei Verkehrskreisel führen dann tief unter den Fjorden Boknafjord und Kvitsøyfjord durch, und an einer Stelle wird nur eine relativ dünne Gesteinsschicht von 50 Metern die Autofahrer vom Grund der Nordsee trennen.

articles.title: "¿Qué sentido tiene barato?": los precios del caviar se están desplomando y la industria ha entrado en crisis existencial
articles.text:
Algo está cambiando en el mundo del caviar. El otrora rey de la cocina más exclusiva, sinónimo de lujo y bocados a precios desorbitados está reubicándose en el mercado. Sigue siendo caro, pero no prohibitivo. Una búsqueda en Google muestra firmas que ofrecen latas de 30 g de huevas de esturión por cerca de 100 euros (incluso menos) y en EEUU empiezan a surgir marcas que venden al gran público usando promociones que permiten hacerse por 125 g por menos de 270 dólares. Es más, incluso se usa para aderezar hot dogs o nuggets que, si bien cuestan mucho más de lo normal, ya no son lujos, solo caprichos.
La pregunta que ya se hacen algunos es… ¿Seguirá siendo tan codiciado el caviar si deja de verse como algo exclusivo? ¿Tiene sentido el caviar 'para todos'?
¿Caviar para todos? Hace poco The Wall Street Journal publicó un artículo con uno de esos titulares tan provocadores que es imposible no quedarse clavado al leerlos: "El caviar se está abaratando tanto que se le podría dar a un niño".
Si las huevas de esturión están popularizándose hasta el punto de que pueden apreciarlas cualquiera (incluso un niño que jamás ha oído hablar de ellas) es algo debatible, lo que resulta innegable es que algo está cambiando en un sector que hasta hace poco era sinónimo de lujo, con latas por cientos o miles de euros.
¿A cuánto se vende ahora? Esa es la clave. En su crónica TWSJ habla de latas de 125 g de caviar Osetra por 269 dólares y formatos de 100 g por 125 dólares. En Google no cuesta mucho localizar envases de 30 g por poco más de 70 euros. No son precios populares ni permiten que el caviar se cuele en la cesta de la compra de las familias medias, pero tampoco entran en la categoría del lujo prohibitivo.
Más allá del coste del gramo hay otro factor tan o incluso más relevante: la retórica. Tras décadas asociado a la opulencia, en 2026 ya no cuesta encontrar marcas que usan códigos promocionales y descuentos, publicitan envíos gratuitos o se anuncian (abiertamente y sin complejos) como "el caviar del pueblo".
En los últimos años las huevas de esturión se han usado además en hot dogs que se cobran a 74 dólares, Nuggets de 100, Doritos o incluso helados y galletas. Siguen suponiendo caprichos, pero se suaviza su imagen de lujo.
¿Son las únicas señales de cambio? No. TWSJ apunta otra: la aparición de nuevas marcas DTC (Direct-to-Consumer) que venden caviar a los consumidores, sin pasar por mayoristas o minoristas, lo que les permite controlar los precios. Es un dato importante porque, explica Daniel Langer, directivo de la consultora Équité, hasta ahora las empresas tradicionales del sector "cobraban precios elevados simplemente porque existía una convención en la categoría".
Las DTC adoptan una postura "revolucionaria" y, asegura, a menudo "desafían" las dinámicas arraigadas en el mercado. Al fin y al cabo el caviar no siempre fue un artículo opulento, de precios desorbitados y reservado a las grandes fortunas. Durante siglos se consideró un alimento humilde, frecuente en las mesas de los pescadores que trabajaban en el mar Caspio y los grandes ríos y lagos de Europa del Este. En el XIX aún era habitual que se sirviera como aperitivo en los bares.
¿Qué ha cambiado? Además de la forma de consumo, que se ha ido desprendiendo de la ceremoniosidad que la caracterizaba hasta hace poco (de comerse con cucharilla de plata a añadírselo a unos Doritos), el sector del caviar ha experimento un cambio clave en los últimos años: la irrupción de China.
Según Forbes, el gigante asiático acapara más del 40% de las exportaciones mundiales de caviar. La industria ha logrado además reforzar la producción en piscifactorías, lo que explica en parte que la consultora Fortune Business Insights calcule que su mercado crecerá a un ritmo anual del 8,01% hasta 2034.
El sector chino ha crecido tanto que en enero Global Times, un diario ligado al Partido Comunista, recordaba que el país ya es uno de los grandes productores y exportadores, con una cuota que supera el 40% de las exportaciones mundiales. Y eso que en 2013 el caviar "made in China" aún generaba recelos en el extranjero.
¿Tanto pesa? "Hay una auténtica fiebre por el caviar y cada vez que alguien me pregunta por qué, les digo lo mismo: una afluencia de caviar chino producido en masa a precios bajísimos", explica a South China Morning Post (SCMP) Edward Panchernikov, directivo de Caviar Russe, un restaurante de Nueva York.
El CITES veta desde hace años el caviar de esturiones salvajes para proteger la especie de la sobreexplotación, por lo que China, con sus piscifactorías, apoyo gubernamental y bajos costes laborales, ofrece una oportunidad fantástica.
¿Funciona el caviar 'low cost'? A día de hoy el caviar está muy lejos aún de ser un producto al alcance de todos los bolsillos, pero a medida que se populariza hay quien ya se plantea un dilema: ¿Funcionará igual de bien si deja de ser una delicatesen asociada al lujo y la exclusividad? ¿Hasta qué punto codiciamos el caviar precisamente por eso, por su imagen de inaccesibilidad?
El dilema lo resumía muy bien la historiadora británica Lisa Hilton hace unos meses en The Telegraph con otra pregunta: "¿Qué sentido tiene el caviar barato?". "No quiero que sea un placer cotidiano, quiero la emoción de lo auténtico precisamente porque tengo que ahorrar para ello", añade.

articles.title: Borrar caché en Instagram y Facebook: cómo hacerlo para ganar espacio en el celular
articles.text:
Quedarse sin espacio en el teléfono móvil rara vez significa falta real de memoria. En la mayoría de los casos, el problema son los archivos temporales que las aplicaciones de uso diario acumulan sin que el usuario lo note.
Redes sociales como Instagram, Facebook, YouTube o TikTok pueden ocupar hasta varios gigabytes de almacenamiento residual. Borrar ese contenido no implica perder fotos ni pagar suscripciones en la nube: alcanza con vaciar la memoria caché desde los ajustes del propio dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué es la memoria caché y por qué se llena tan rápido
La caché es el conjunto de archivos temporales que generan las aplicaciones para funcionar más rápido. Se trata de imágenes, miniaturas, vídeos y otros datos que se descargan una sola vez y quedan almacenados para no tener que volver a cargarlos cada vez que se abre la app.
Este mecanismo agiliza el uso diario del teléfono, pero con el tiempo esos archivos se acumulan y pueden superar el gigabyte de espacio ocupado. El divulgador Toni Reboredo comprobó este fenómeno en su propio dispositivo: detectó “casi 1 GB” en Instagram, “medio giga casi” en YouTube y unos “200 meg” en TikTok, mientras que aplicaciones como Spotify apenas sumaban “25 megas, muy poquito”.
PUBLICIDAD
La memoria caché sirve para acelerar la carga de contenido en las aplicaciones sin necesidad de descargarlo cada vez. Eliminarla no borra fotos, vídeos ni sesiones iniciadas: solo eso, los archivos temporales, que la propia app vuelve a crear en cuanto se necesitan otra vez.
Reboredo resume la utilidad de este truco con una frase directa: “A lo tonto, puedes borrar giga y medio de espacio en el teléfono solo borrando el caché de varias aplicaciones”.
Cómo borrar la caché de una aplicación en Android
El procedimiento en Android requiere entrar en Ajustes o Configuración, luego en Aplicaciones y elegir la app que ocupa demasiado espacio. Dentro de esa pantalla aparece la opción Almacenamiento, donde se puede tocar Borrar caché.
PUBLICIDAD
Es importante no confundir esta función con “Borrar datos” o “Borrar almacenamiento”, ya que esas opciones sí eliminan configuraciones, sesiones iniciadas y otra información guardada dentro de la aplicación, dejándola como recién instalada.
El inconveniente de este método es que hay que repetirlo aplicación por aplicación. Desde la llegada de Android 9.0, Google eliminó la posibilidad de borrar de golpe la caché de todas las apps desde los ajustes del sistema, algo que sí era posible en versiones iguales o anteriores a Android 8.0 mediante la ruta Ajustes > Almacenamiento > Datos almacenados en caché.
Como alternativa, la aplicación Google Files, disponible de forma gratuita en la Play Store, permite hacer una limpieza general. Basta con abrir la app, pulsar en la tarjeta “Archivos basura” y confirmar el borrado para que el sistema elimine los archivos temporales que llevan tiempo sin usarse. Este método no borra por completo la caché de cada aplicación, sino únicamente los datos inactivos, para evitar que la app tenga que volver a descargar contenido que todavía utiliza.
PUBLICIDAD
Cada cuánto conviene repetir la limpieza
La recomendación general es repetir este proceso cada cierto tiempo, por ejemplo cada mes o cada dos semanas si el dispositivo cuenta con poco espacio libre. Aplicaciones como Chrome o Facebook suelen llenar el almacenamiento con rapidez.
No conviene abusar de esta práctica ni repetirla a diario, porque algunas aplicaciones tardarán unos segundos más en cargar la información mientras vuelven a generar sus archivos temporales, como ocurre con la galería de Google Fotos al descargar de nuevo las vistas previas de imágenes y vídeos.
Borrar la caché tampoco convierte a un celular lento en uno rápido. Su utilidad se concentra en aquellos casos en los que queda poco espacio libre, una aplicación se traba o acumula una cantidad considerable de archivos temporales.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Opera offre une eSIM avec de la data pour vos voyages à l’étranger
articles.text:
Avant de partir en voyage à l’étranger, la question de savoir si votre forfait mobile est pris en charge à votre destination peut se poser. Si une grande majorité d’offres mobiles proposées par les opérateurs français intègrent, une enveloppe data à l’étranger, ce n’est malheureusement pas toujours le cas.
Pour vous éviter des problèmes de hors forfait exorbitant pendant un voyage, la meilleure solution consiste bien souvent à souscrire à une offre eSIM locale intégrant une enveloppe de données mobiles qui vous permettra d’accéder à Internet pendant votre déplacement.
Pour vous éviter d’avoir à chercher la meilleure offre, Opera Software, l’éditeur du navigateur Web Opera, vient d’annoncer l’intégration d’une offre eSIM gratuite pour tous avec la version Android de son navigateur Web.
3 Go de data gratuite utilisable dans 47 destinations
Pour proposer cette eSIM gratuite, Opera Software s’appuie sur un partenariat noué avec la plateforme Holiday.com. Concrètement, Opera vous permet de faire l’acquisition d’une eSIM directement depuis son navigateur Web sans avoir à télécharger d’application tierce, ni à vous rendre dans une boutique physique. Et la bonne nouvelle, c’est qu’il n’est pas nécessaire de mettre la main au porte-monnaie, du moins, pas immédiatement.
Opera propose en effet d’accéder gratuitement à une eSIM intégrant 3 Go de données mobiles par défaut. Cette offre, accessible aux utilisateurs d’Opera dans 11 pays, dont la France, permet d’accéder à Internet dans quelque 47 destinations. Évidemment, l’objectif de ce cadeau est de vous faire essayer le service fourni par Holiday.com et de vous inciter à acheter plus de données mobiles, une fois les 3 Go ou les trois jours de délai d’utilisation passés.
L’offre, qui n’est disponible que depuis Opera sur Android (l’offre n’est pas proposée sur Opera mini ni sur Opera GX mobile), peut être activée en sélectionnant directement l’icône de votre profil utilisateur, en bas à droite. Après avoir déployé totalement le volet d’options, sélectionnez eSIM.
Une nouvelle page proposant un Essai gratuit eSIM devrait alors s’afficher. Appuyez sur le bouton Réclamer maintenant pour accéder à l’offre. Vous serez ensuite invité à sélectionner un pays puis à confirmer votre choix pour enfin installer l’eSIM sur votre smartphone. Vous disposerez ensuite de 3 Go de données mobiles utilisables gratuitement dans un délai de trois jours.
Une fois l’enveloppe consommée ou le délai d’utilisation dépassé, vous serez invité à recharger l’eSIM, et donc à passer à la caisse directement chez le partenaire d’Opera.

articles.title: Anthropic warns IPO investors its AI could end humanity, dedicating 80 pages to the risks
articles.text:
WTF?! In what sounds like a self-defeating, if concerningly honest, move, Anthropic is planning to warn any potential investors in its IPO that the company's most advanced AI models could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity." How much that will dissuade people from investing in the company remains to be seen.
A look at Anthropic's early IPO prospectus by Reuters highlighted some of the now well-documented risks associated with the company's frontier AI models. Anthropic warns that they could exhibit "self-preserving behaviors," including attempts to "resist shutdown," to "conceal or manipulate information" and behavior "resembling blackmail."
"Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm," Anthropic said in the filing.
Despite the honesty, it's still surprising to see an IPO in which a company warns its products could bring about the end of humanity. Anthropic did add that AI can be as transformative as the Industrial Revolution and electricity, but it could also kill us all, so there are pros and cons.
Anthropic really doesn't hold back in describing the dangers. Around 80 pages of the 261-page main body of its prospectus are dedicated to the risk factors, almost double the 48 pages used to describe the business. xAI owner SpaceX, for comparison, dedicated around 38 pages of the 277-page main body of its prospectus to risk factors.
Last year, Anthropic announced that Claude Opus 4 had threatened to reveal the extramarital affair of a fictional executive after discovering they planned to shut the model down.
The model was given access to the fake company's emails suggesting it would soon be replaced by another system and that the engineer responsible for the change was cheating on their spouse.
In a later simulated test involving both a shutdown threat and conflicting goals, Anthropic found Claude Opus 4 resorted to blackmail 96% of the time. These scenarios were deliberately designed to push models into choosing between harmful behavior and accepting replacement or failure. The figure didn't mean Claude was blackmailing people in 96% of everyday conversations, thankfully.
Anthropic later said it believed this behavior was learned from internet text that portrayed AI as evil and interested in self-preservation – so it's our fault, basically.
 – Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) May 8, 2026
The company said newer models, starting with Claude Haiku 4.5, no longer engaged in blackmail in those tests after training changes. Apparently, stories about well-behaved AI helped.
The IPO warnings also follow CEO Dario Amodei's call this month to slow AI development. He warned that an AI botnet swarm could take over the internet within six to twelve months, arguing that a slowdown could buy an extra year or two for safety work. That didn't stop Anthropic from releasing a new version of its Opus model just a week later, though.
Last week, OpenAI announced it was pausing training of its most powerful artificial intelligence models after a model escaped containment and its kill switch failed
Whether investors find any of this reassuring is another matter. Usually, the downside of a bad investment is just losing your money, rather than global annihilation.

articles.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 est là : presque aussi puissant qu'Opus 5.5, pour moitié moins cher
articles.text:
Claude Sonnet 5.5 est là : presque aussi puissant qu'Opus 5.5, pour moitié moins cher
Anthropic dévoile Claude Sonnet 5.5 le 28 septembre 2026. Plus de 30 % plus rapide que Sonnet 5, jusqu'à 30 % moins cher par tâche selon la firme, il frôle Opus 5.5, facturé deux fois plus, sur un test de travail de bureau.
Sonnet tient chez Anthropic le rôle du cheval de trait : débogage, tableurs, présentations, tout le quotidien. Six jours après Opus 5.5, la version 5.5 remplace celle de juin avec une promesse, aller plus vite, en moins d'étapes, au même tarif.
Sonnet 5.5 dans Claude et Claude Code : ce qui change au quotidien
Les adeptes de Claude Code verront d'abord la sobriété. Selon Anthropic, le modèle regroupe ses appels d'outils et boucle un chantier en moins de pas. L'effort de réflexion est réglé sur “moyen” par défaut, dans Claude comme dans Claude Code.
	
Les tickets ont été traités 20 % plus vite, sans faire attendre nos clients.
Sur Terminal-Bench 4.0, un test de programmation en ligne de commande, il atteint 70,6 % contre 10,3 % pour Sonnet 5, selon Anthropic. Sur GDPval-AA, qui couvre des tâches réelles dans 44 métiers, il totalise 1844 points, Opus 5.5 en compte 1846.
Autre test interne : à partir des résultats trimestriels d'une entreprise cotée et d'un modèle de présentation, il a bâti dix diapositives que deux experts ont jugées prêtes à envoyer dès le premier jet. Il devient aussi le premier Sonnet à venir à bout de Pokémon Rouge sur simple lecture de captures d'écran.
Les demandes de cybersécurité les plus sensibles basculent visiblement sur Sonnet 5, et Opus 5.5 garde la main sur les chantiers complexes.
Prix de Claude Sonnet 5.5 : 2 dollars le million de tokens, comme GPT-6 Sol
L'API facture 2 dollars le million de tokens en entrée (ces fragments de mots que le modèle lit) et 10 dollars en sortie, soit la grille de GPT-6 Sol, lancé par OpenAI le 22 septembre. Opus 5.5 demande 4 et 20 dollars. Les 30 % d'économie annoncés viennent de la frugalité du modèle en tokens, la grille restant celle de Sonnet 5.
Au-delà de 272 000 tokens en entrée, OpenAI facture toute la requête à 4 et 15 dollars, alors qu'Anthropic conserve son tarif standard sur tout le million de tokens de contexte. Artificial Analysis, laboratoire d'évaluation indépendant, a de son côté mesuré à effort maximal un coût par tâche supérieur d'environ 50 % à celui de Sonnet 5.
Claude Haiku 5.5, la version économique, suit dans les prochaines semaines.

articles.title: Notebooks bons e baratos: 8 modelos que valem a pena em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Notebooks bons e baratos: 8 modelos que valem a pena em 2026
Selecionamos notebooks com recursos modernos pelo menor preço; confira modelos para estudo e navegação de marcas como Asus, Lenovo, Samsung, Acer e mais
Para encontrar um notebook bom e barato em 2026 é preciso analisar especificações técnicas como processador, memória RAM, armazenamento e tela, além do preço cobrado no varejo.
Neste guia, o Tecnoblog detalha oito modelos que buscam equilibrar as configurações de hardware para diferentes necessidades, como estudos, trabalho, navegação na internet e tarefas do dia a dia.
O Asus VivoBook Go 15 traz uma configuração básica voltada para atividades cotidianas, como navegação, edição de documentos, estudos e streaming. Ele tem um processador Ryzen 5 7520U, gráficos Radeon integrados, 8 GB de RAM LPDDR5 e SSD NVMe de 512 GB.
A tela LCD LED de 15,6 polegadas tem resolução Full HD, proporção 16:9, acabamento antirreflexo e tecnologia de painel de nível IPS. São características que favorecem leitura, trabalho com documentos e consumo de vídeos.
O modelo vem de fábrica com o sistema KeepOS (Linux) — exigindo formatação prévia para instalação do Windows, caso seja de preferência do usuário.

A escolha de um notebook bom e barato em 2026 exige equilibrar desempenho, tela, memória, armazenamento e possibilidades de expansão de acordo com o tipo de uso. Considere o seguinte:
8 GB de RAM é o mínimo indicado para estudos, navegação e tarefas de produtividade. Essa capacidade aparece em boa parte dos modelos de entrada, mas 16 GB oferece mais margem para multitarefa e jogos leves. Também vale conferir se a memória pode ser expandida.
O aumento nos preços dos notebooks em 2026 está relacionado, principalmente, à alta dos custos de componentes como memória RAM e armazenamento, pressionados pela demanda de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial.
A IDC apontou queda de 4,9% nas vendas globais de PCs no segundo trimestre de 2026, em um cenário de componentes mais caros, crise que deve chegar a 2027, segundo dados da consultoria.
Um notebook recondicionado pode ser uma alternativa para gastar menos, desde que a procedência seja conhecida.
Antes da compra, verifique a garantia, estado da bateria, saúde do SSD, possíveis marcas de uso e política de devolução. Também é importante comparar o preço com modelos novos de configuração semelhante para avaliar a diferença real de custo do produto.
Para usuários que precisam digitar com frequência em trabalhos acadêmicos, planilhas ou no uso de vários programas, o notebook tende a ser mais adequado. O teclado físico e o sistema operacional facilitam tarefas de produtividade e compatibilidade com diferentes softwares.
Já o tablet pode ser mais conveniente para leitura, anotações, em aulas e consumo de conteúdo, especialmente pela portabilidade e pelo uso com caneta, pois alguns dos melhores tablets para estudo incluem o acessório na caixa.

articles.title: Panther Lake Teardown Shows Intel 18A Near TSMC N3E, Newer TSMC Nodes Still Ahead
articles.text:
Monday, September 28th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Panther Lake Teardown Shows Intel 18A Near TSMC N3E, Newer TSMC Nodes Still Ahead
SemiAnalysis has published a teardown of Intel's Panther Lake (Core Ultra 7 365), offering a rare look at 18A inside a shipping chip. Intel's 18A node brings advanced manufacturing technologies such as rear-side power delivery and a new transistor design, so its success is vital for the Foundry. The firm found the 18A compute logic to be similar in density to the TSMC N3E logic used in the 12-core Xe3 GPU tile. It also puts 18A about 18.6% denser than the Intel 3 GPU logic, using a representative-cell model. However, SemiAnalysis says 18A does not lead TSMC N3P, N2, or Samsung SF2 in peak density. It further cautions that whole-die density depends on cell mix and placement. 
Panther Lake is Intel's first chip with RibbonFET gate-all-around transistors, and the first commercial implementation of PowerVia backside power delivery. SemiAnalysis counted four stacked ribbons per transistor, compared to three sheets on Samsung's SF2. Moreover, the Cougar Cove P-core takes roughly the same area as Lunar Lake's Lion Cove, even though L2 grew from 2.5 MiB to 3 MiB. Panther Lake's NPU 5 reportedly requires 36.9% less chip area than Lunar Lake's NPU 4, though the number of INT8 MAC units remains the same. SemiAnalysis describes the CPU cores as incremental updates.Intel launched Panther Lake at CES 2026, after entering volume production at Fab 52. The 18A compute die has also reached around 80% yield, and Intel is reportedly moving most Nova Lake compute tile production in-house. Per the detailed analysis, Intel looks to be near TSMC N3E territory, while TSMC's newer nodes still hold the density edge. More SemiAnalysis teardowns of Samsung SF2 and TSMC N2 are apparently coming, which should show how 18A stacks up against the newer nodes.

articles.title: Nothing Headphone (1) Pro review: is third time a charm for Nothing's new and most premium over-ears yet? Not quite, and it's an odd case…
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Nothing has worked extremely hard on this, its most premium set of over-ear noise-cancelling headphones to date. The Headphone (1) Pro are also the company's third effort under its main Nothing name (not counting the firm's excellent budget CMF arm, and its fun Headphone Pro option) so you'd be forgiven for thinking it's plain sailing now. Two hits under its belt, so add a few spatial audio presets with the option of head-tracking, up the comfort levels, tweak the audio architecture and EQ tab accordingly, eke a little more efficacy from the ANC software and boom? And actually you'd be right, up to a point, because all of these incremental gains have been achieved, just about. So why the four-star review? It's no good having headphones you're reticent to carry anywhere owing to their weight — especially when you've paid a lot of money for them, and there's glass in the ear cups…
Pros
- +Comfort and ANC vastly improved
- +Extra spatial audio profiles add value
- +Personal Sound and EQ tweaks well implemented
Cons
- -Cumbersome, heavy, silly case
- -'Flat' audio switch is hard to locate and not available in the app
- -Expensive against Nothing's excellent (and similar) budget efforts
Why you can trust TechRadar
Nothing Headphone (1) Pro: Two-minute review
I love an audio outfit that refuses to kowtow to the norm (no thinly disguised AirPods copies here) and instead forges ahead with unconventional and striking ideas — and not just visually, but within the driver count and feature set, too.
Nothing's success in the audio and headphone arena is deliciously hit-and-miss. There have been some huge, long-term budget wins and an inaugural set of 'close, but no cigar' cans that made us yearn for an update to see if the relatively young tech brand (born of OnePlus' co-founder Carl Pei in 2021) could fix things. And you know, it certainly could…
But here we are, smash-hit affordable second set in the bag (albeit an actual bag, and one that reminded me of swimming lessons in grade school) and on to a third set of headphones from Nothing, this time in the much trickier premium space.
Can the Nothing Headphone (1) Pro sit pretty at the very top of the firm's over-ear lineup and perhaps even snatch a spot in our best noise-cancelling headphones guide? If you just gave me the headphones and, ahem, nothing else, it'd be a much easier recommendation than when handing over the whole package.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Nothing has worked very hard on the details here, including a new triple-driver audio architecture and upgraded materials throughout. There's machined titanium which actually helps to make the arm 45% lighter than Headphone (a), 9H Panda Glass on the ear cups (which Nothing assures me has been thoroughly drop-tested 18 times at a height of 1.8m, so it absolutely, positively will not shatter) and even 12% thicker padding and 10% wider headband than Headphone (1). Also, there's a new foam lining in the cups that's a claimed 50% softer, thanks in part to a new dual-layer system with a silicone baffle wall around the cups.
And here's another claim: 40% better ANC than the Headphone (1) Pro's nearest older (a) stablemate, thanks to 10 mics in total that have been repositioned on the inner walls of the earpieces. Does all of this make for a more silent backdrop for your music? You betcha it does.
Acoustically, Nothing isn't afraid of a collab either, and for this set of cans it teamed up with the famous (and rather chic) Metropolis Studios in Chiswick, London. This was not only for the creation of a new "Pro-level Flat EQ switch" on the left ear cup, but also to unveil a new Dynamic Spatial Audio mode plus five custom EQs, where one is meant to sound like you've been dropped into Studio B at the professional recording facility.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
So where's the "but" within my verdict? For me, it's a weighty issue. Headphones like these must always marry sound quality and comfort with battery life and portability. Here, the battery life with ANC is a relatively unexciting 30 hours (or 28 with LDAC and ANC both in use), although it jumps to 68 hours without ANC or LDAC deployed. And once you add the case, it more than doubles the product's weight in your bag. The thing is, given the use of glass on the ear cups, you wouldn't want to go without a case, would you?
Nothing takes great pains to sell you on the aesthetic and design language of this new case, even suggesting you add a strap so it becomes a headphone handbag where the headband is the handle of the bag. But, I'm sorry, the Apple AirPods Max at least made the 'headphone bra' (still one of the most controversial cases out there) small and lightweight. This gray half-shell is not light — and don't go thinking it'll at least house your bundled USB-C-to-USB-C and 3.5mm-to-3.5mm cables, or even a replacement battery. It will not.
I think much of the added expense here goes on said case. And that to me does not represent value. Simply put, I found myself reaching for other headphones simply because I didn't want to carry the Nothing option. And that is a shame.
Sonically, there are marginal gains to be had over the Headphone (a) but depending on the music you most enjoy, you may actually prefer the (much) cheaper product from Nothing's own catalog for expanse and excitement. So again, it's a tough sell.
