articles.title: The 10 best movies I saw at TIFF 2026
articles.text:
While I’m known as the “gaming guy” at MobileSyrup, my second great love is film. For me, there’s nothing as sacred as going into a theatre, silencing my phone, and locking into a cinematic journey for a couple of hours.
The Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), in many ways, is the purest distillation of that. With a bunch of the films having their world premieres at the event, there’s such a sense of discovery as you go in almost completely blind. Naturally, this can lead to you more than a few stinkers, but it can also be so exciting when you come across a real winner.
Now, I’ll confess that TIFF 2026 definitely felt softer compared to last year’s big 50th anniversary show, with many of the nearly 30 films I saw simply being mediocre at best. But if nothing else, that just made what did hit have all the more impact.
Here are my 10 favourite films from TIFF 2026.
10. Babies
Director: Lauren Miller Rogen
Release date: TBA 2027
People have always been very weird about Vancouver funnyman Seth Rogen and wife Lauren Miller’s openness about not wanting to have kids. (It’s a completely understandable choice and also totally not anyone else’s business either way!) And so, I greatly admire how Lauren Miller was inspired to write and direct this comedy-drama unpacking those very feelings. The film follows Annie (Anna Kendrick) and Aaron (Seth), a couple of 17 years that’s long been apprehensive about becoming parents, only for them to have to directly confront that dilemma when their recently separated friend Eliza (Kate Berlant) and her toddler move in with them.
Babies mines this less-than-ideal situation for a lot of warm-hearted humour not only about the couple’s insecurities and awkwardness, but also the unexpected happiness they experience as circumstances bring them closer to their friend and her kid. And through this, many valid points are raised on both sides of the “Should we have kids?” debate, with Lauren Miller’s snappy screenplay being more than fair as it meaningfully explores them all. Not all of the subplots with their larger group of friends and family work, mind you, but one focused on Annie’s family dealing with her mother’s Alzheimer’s is genuinely touching, no doubt due to this being another topic that’s near and dear to the Rogens’ hearts.
It’s those personal touches that make this such a delightful (and ever-timely) film.
9. The Beloved
Director: Rodrigo Sorogoyen
Release date: TBA
I kept seeing TIFF ads describing this as a “darker Sentimental Value,” which was my favourite movie from last year. In some ways, that pitch is accurate, but The Beloved is also a different beast entirely. In this Spanish-language drama, an acclaimed director attempts to reconnect with his estranged daughter by casting her in his latest film, which is, admittedly, the same premise as Sentimental Value.
But I also appreciated how Javier Bardem’s Esteban Martínez does indeed have a darker side to him, taking out his insecurities on his daughter Emilia (Victoria Luengo) and the rest of the cast and crew in frightening ways that are reminiscent of J.K. Simmons’ Fletcher from Whiplash. It’s a rich exploration of the ripple effects of unresolved pain while also serving as a fine entry in the “movie about filmmaking” subgenre. All the while, Emilia makes for a compelling lead as she’s decidedly more emotionally guarded than Renate Reinsve’s Nora from Sentimental Value, giving her confrontations with Esteban a tense, powder-keg sort of feeling. This all culminates in a finale that is both deeply cathartic yet also open-ended in a believably human way.
It’s not quite on the level of Sentimental Value, but it’s a strong film nonetheless, led by Bardem and Luengo’s stirring performances.
8. How We Stand 🍁
Director: Marie Clements
Release date: TBA
Adapting her 2012 play Tombs of the Vanishing Indian, Vancouver-born Métis multi-hyphenate Marie Clements delivers a powerful tribute to the many Indigenous women who had to endure relocation and sterilization at the hands of the government. Following three sisters who were separated as kids after police killed her mother, the film meaningfully explores the various and often disparate paths that these women had to take, all while dealing with insidious forms of everyday racism.
I was particularly taken by the story of the sister who’s played by Fort McMurray-born Cree actress Alyssa Wapanatâhk (Peter Pan & Wendy), who masks her pain with a dry wit and flirtatiousness as she navigates the Hollywood system. Clements also brings a vivid visual language to the film, with rich, natural cinematography and some inspired heightened elements and scene transitions that lend a sense of spirituality that unites the sisters and their mother across time and space. The final scene, in particular, is genuinely moving.
A beautiful, crucial film.
7. Everytime
Director: Sandra Wollner
Release date: TBA
Given that so much media is about grief nowadays (honestly, fair), I respect Sandra Wollner for taking a much more methodical and subdued approach. Indeed, there are very few overtly emotional scenes despite the inherent tragedy at the centre of this German psychological drama, with Wollner instead relying on vivid, natural imagery captured in long, often listless takes. This mesmerizing, hypnotic sensation, as captured by Aftersun director of photography Gregory Oke, really helps convey the feeling that life simply goes on as people have to contend with their grief in different ways, even as that enduring pain can hit you especially hard at any given moment.
All the while, the film explores how technology preserves the essence of people in very particular moments and places before the much more abstract finale in the stunning Canary Island of Tenerife deliberately upends that sense of time and space. These scenes almost feel like they come out of nowhere but are nonetheless consistent with the themes of the movie, especially with respect to the seemingly opposed motifs of real, gorgeous nature and the cozy digital simulacrum with which the kids are obsessed.
Who’d have thought one of the standouts of TIFF would incorporate Minecraft in such a profound and poignant way?
6. La Bola Negra
Director: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (known collectively as “Los Javis”)
Release date: Dec. 4, 2026 (Netflix)
An exquisitely well-made Spanish drama that tells a deeply touching story about queer repression that fascinatingly spans three distinct time periods. Discovering how they both thematically and narratively connect proves to be a compelling hook, although at close to three hours, it can feel overlong and choppy, especially in its drawn-out conclusion.
Still, it’s a lovely, poignant film, with a sense of timeless poeticism that weaves together the lives of our three leads. Notably, this Spanish drama took home the TIFF’s People’s Choice Award, which means that it was voted by audiences to be the best overall film of the festival while also signifying major Oscar potential. All of that success is well-deserved.
5. Fjord
Director: Cristian Mungiu
Release date: Oct. 9, 2026 (theatres)
A morally complex issue surrounding the parenting of a Romanian-Norwegian couple (Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve) paves the way for a thought-provoking examination of family values and cultural norms with salient critiques of those on various sides of the political spectrum. But rather than simply going for a lazy “both sides” stance, Fjord uses this framework to unpack how our many hypocrisies have led us to the divisive climate in which we find ourselves. There are shades of Justine Triet’s stellar Anatomy of a Fall in Mungiu’s approach to crafting nuanced courtroom drama, but he also employs a commendable level of restraint.
Indeed, Fjord is much more of a slow burn, ratcheting up the innate discomfort not through a riotous yet thematically relevant cover of a 50 Cent song or explosive performances by the leads, but rather by making everything more unsettling, in its own way, by showing how mundane it all is. This is the new normal: how casually we are all so quick to tear each other apart based on what we deem as “right.”
Eerily timely, tightly directed, sharply written and impeccably acted by Stan, Reinsve and co., Fjord is easily one of the best movies of the year.
4. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
Director: Bassam Tariq
Release date: Oct. 9, 2026 (theatres)
People were describing this as “Muslim John Wick,” but I honestly think that does this a disservice. Instead, writer-director Bassam Tariq is far more interested in this being a beautifully spiritual family drama about hitman Latif (Mahershala Ali) trying to raise his kids after the loss of his wife. Having his core struggles centred around efforts to juggle his (tenuous) commitment to his Muslim faith with the increasingly desperate quest (inspired by Tariq’s own life) to simply find breast milk for his baby makes for such a refreshing and even soulful take on the classic “assassin action movie.”
Indeed, the scenes in which Latif simply talks with his kids and community feel so lovingly sincere, in no small part due to a sensational Ali, who conveys so much pain and inner strife in simple gazes. (Special shoutout as well to Adia, who is fantastic as Latif’s daughter who’s had to grow up so fast and become a surrogate mother within the family.)
And I adore how Tariq so thoughtfully explores religion — not only with the appropriate nuance associated with someone being a “Muslim hitman,” but also in the ways in which it can simultaneously be weaponized by fanatics like John Cho’s manic Hwan while also connecting us in the hands of someone more benevolent. In fact, one of YMYMYM’s most lovingly understated moments is when Latif and his family take refuge with a neighbouring Bible study group. A lesser film would have made this a source of conflict between two ideologies (or worse still, make this about how one is “better” than the other), but here, instead, it’s a touching reminder of what unites instead of divides us. (All the while, the film also manages to be surprisingly very funny, with a running joke about Latif grappling with the concept of furries, in particular, that had our screening hollering.)
And yes, we also get some action, and it’s snappily directed by Tariq. It’s not flashy or gratuitous, simply feeling raw, grounded and believably bloody, as befitting of a man who doesn’t relish in what he’s doing. But YMYMYM is very much at its best when it’s grounded in Latif’s familial woes, and thankfully, that makes up most of the runtime. I’m so glad that Ali and Tariq got to make something so deeply engrossing, personal and profound after Marvel so embarrassingly failed them with Blade.
3. Wild Horse Nine
Director: Martin McDonagh
Release date: Nov. 6, 2026
In Bruges is one of my all-time favourite movies, so I knew I had to see McDonagh’s spiritual successor to his 2008 classic. And certainly, Wild Horse Nine is conceptually and thematically very similar to In Bruges, following two trained killers as they reflect upon their sins in a paradisial setting while their demanding and cantankerous boss looms above them. But Wild Horse Nine makes some clever twists to that formula that really worked for me.
For one, John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell are simply phenomenal here, and their relationship provides some glorious inversions on the one from In Bruges between Colin Farrell and Brendan Gleeson’s world-weary gunmen. What’s more, Malkovich’s existential woes are given greater, more tangible weight by the film’s implication of him in many real-world assassinations, adding a rich political subtext to the film. Wild Horse Nine doesn’t absolve him of these CIA-sanctioned murders, but rather uses them to deepen the sense of nihilism he’s experiencing and, in turn, make his fleeting moments of optimism and compassion in his sweet relationship with Mariana di Girolamo‘s wide-eyed liberal Chilean all the more impactful.
And without spoiling anything, the film proves even more melancholic, in some ways, than In Bruges, with an early plot revelation hanging over the film like an ominous dark cloud. All of that works wonderfully with McDonagh’s usual blend of riotous black comedy, which is particularly sharp here. A worthy successor to In Bruges and a brilliant film in its own right.
2. Sunburn 🍁
Director: Serville Poblete
Release date: TBA
As anyone from Toronto will tell you, it can get real hot here in the summer. But as writer-director Serville Poblete so beautifully portrays in Sunburn, summers in the city are also so magical. As one of the most multicultural places in the world, the sense of community here is resolutely strong, transcending race and age and sexuality and affluence. And during the sweltering heat, you’ll see people from all of these disparate backgrounds coming together for street markets and concerts and comedy shows and strolls in the park and the like. Through the high-rise setting of St. James Town, Sunburn celebrates community in such a loving way that it genuinely moved me to tears. It’s all in the way that Poblete so artfully captures the goofy innocence and soulful yearning of this eclectic cast of kids, all written and acted in such a natural way that I felt like they were actually my own friends.
And Poblete uses their interactions for deeper, universal themes that hit particularly hard. Summer, of course, is also a period of transition, marking the end of one school year and ringing in the start of another, with all of the life changes that come with that. Moving away against your wishes, leaving behind that childhood friend. Choosing to move away to leave behind that childhood pain. Reflecting on the absence of a loved one taken far too soon.
There’s such an aching, youthful wistfulness underneath all of Sunburn that everyone can relate to here, and Poblete, exhibiting a masterful directorial hand, knows exactly when to let it wash over you through vivid, warm, soothing imagery and actors’ sincere, subdued expressions that say more than dialogue ever could. In these moments, I felt like I was right there with them, solemnly awaiting wherever life may take us next. But then you see all of the kids together, quietly taking in the fireworks with wide-eyed smiles on their faces, and you remember that’s what makes it all worthwhile.
The fact that Poblete accomplishes all of this in a lean 82 minutes is nothing short of remarkable. A hilarious and deeply moving tribute to community, adolescence and Toronto as a whole. What an unbelievably strong filmmaker voice, and he’s absolutely one I will be on the lookout for from here on out. Not only a TIFF highlight, but one of my favourite movies of the year and an all-timer Canadian film, to boot.
Also, shoutout to the Guyanese guy. Finally some representation besides George in Metal Gear Rising.
1. Josephine
Director: Beth de Araújo
Release date: Nov. 20, 2026
A devastating family drama about a child trying to make sense of a horrifying incident and her ill-equipped parents desperately trying to help her cope with it. It’s a poignant, sobering and deeply empathetic examination of how suddenly youthful innocence can be stripped away, no matter how much we may wish otherwise. Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan are sublime as the struggling father and mother who approach their daughter’s anguish in different yet equally understandable ways, as messy and flawed as they are. But newcomer Mason Reeves is the true star here, magnificently capturing the complicated swell of emotions of a child who’s tragically forced to grapple with something so sinister and traumatic. There are no easy answers here, no convenient playbook to follow, and this trio conveys that sense of heartbreaking exasperation so wonderfully.
Meanwhile, de Araújo, who also penned the tight, contemplative screenplay, exhibits such an astoundingly firm handle on the material, being explicit and even shocking where appropriate while knowing when to exhibit much more restraint and sensitivity. There are some particularly inspired moments in which the camera dizzyingly spins around the house during a pivotal conversation or ping-pongs between prosecutors in court, and they do a stellar job of putting you in the disorienting, frantic and frankly terrifying headspace of the family. All the while, Miles Ross’ sombre score deftly swings between subdued tones and almost operatic crescendos, making the weight of the story completely wash over you like the nearby San Francisco Bay waves.
An incredibly heavy but nonetheless profoundly moving film. Easily my favourite of the festival and one of my top films of 2026, period.
For more on TIFF 2026, check out my review of the Elon Musk documentary and round-up of Canadian films I saw.

articles.title: Microsoft says it loves AMD, just not enough to put it in a new Surface device
articles.text:
The big picture: Microsoft debuted its new Surface Laptop and Surface Pro convertible at Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit event in Maui last week and confirmed that the "Copilot+ PC" branding is being retired for new Windows devices. The company has now offered a rather unconvincing explanation for why the latest Surface devices won't ship with AMD processors.
During an interview with Windows Central, Microsoft's CVP for Surface devices, Brett Ostrum, was asked why the company dropped AMD from its 2026 Surface lineup. Ostrum stated that Microsoft's limited Surface portfolio prevents it from offering too many processor choices, even though it greatly values its relationship with AMD.
According to Ostrum, "We love working with AMD. We have a limited portfolio, and so we have to make our choices pretty wisely in terms of what we're doing and where we're doing." He added that AMD is a valued partner for Microsoft, and that the two companies will continue working closely on other products in the future.
Ostrum did not confirm whether future Surface devices will ship with AMD chips, but online speculation suggests that AMD-powered Surface PCs could still be in the pipeline, with Microsoft rumored to be working on new devices powered by AMD's upcoming Arm chip, codenamed Sound Wave.
The latest Surface devices notwithstanding, Microsoft and AMD share a close working relationship across PCs, gaming consoles, and handhelds. Team Red's 3D V-Cache CPUs remain among the best gaming processors on the market, and the company is also Redmond's chosen partner to supply a custom processor for the next-generation Xbox console, codenamed Project Helix.
Microsoft's new Surface Pro and Surface Laptop may not ship with the Copilot+ branding, but they still offer the same AI features as their predecessors. They're powered by the Snapdragon X2 Plus SoC, which the company claims offers up to 18% greater battery efficiency, over 60% faster graphics performance, and 95% faster on-device AI inference compared with the Snapdragon X Plus.
Alongside the Surface devices, Microsoft also debuted the second-generation Surface Mouse last week. Priced at $79.99, it offers several new features, including haptic feedback, a customizable Action Button, Bluetooth 6.0 with multi-device support, and a claimed six-month battery life. It will go on sale October 13 in Black and Platinum colorways.

articles.title: UK government tells staff to stop thanking AI chatbots — draft guidance pushes lightweight models and shorter prompts to cut environmental impact
articles.text:
UK government tells staff to stop thanking AI chatbots — draft guidance pushes lightweight models and shorter prompts to cut environmental impact
It's more efficient not to say thank you, and there's just no need to, the document explains, alongside other best practices.
The United Kingdom government has published a guide on how its employees should use AI, including a reminder that people don't need to thank their chatbots for their work. The new document, which is still a draft and yet to be finalized, is designed to help people use AI "safely, fairly and sustainably, especially for government work."
The draft "Using AI ethically and sustainably" document also warns users that they should check and follow any AI policies put in place by their individual departments, noting that there may be specific tools and approaches that they should use. It's unclear which departments these may be, but it suggests an awareness that usage patterns may change depending on the nature of the work being done. This is backed up by a section that reminds employees to use the right tool for the task. Examples include using Gemini Flash instead of Gemini Pro and GPT Instant instead of GPT Thinking.
The sub-600-word document offers guidance on using AI responsibly, including checking the output of an AI before using it. This doesn't just apply to making sure that any actual data the AI provides is correct, but also includes ensuring that "users or groups are treated fairly and equally" as well as avoiding "stereotypes or discriminatory language."
The government is also keen to make sure that its employees don't rely on AI, reminding everyone that they are responsible for any content or decisions that are made using the input of AI. They won't be able to simply point the finger at an AI-powered tool if something goes awry. This is especially notable given a recent report suggested that using AI can actually increase burnout because it allows workers to take on too many tasks.
The "Use AI efficiently" section is where the document aims to help reduce the environmental impact of AI use — including a reminder that users need not say thank you. Further, they're told that they should use as few prompts as possible while ensuring they are as short, clear, and direct as possible. There's also a (dead) link to a prompt library. It's possible that the link is only available to those on a government network.
It is, of course, true that you don't need to thank a chatbot for its help, but some may choose to ignore that advice. Especially given constant claims by AI companies that their tech "could kill all humans" sooner or later.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Oliver Haslam has written about technology of all shapes and sizes for over 15 years, both online and in print. He's fascinated by how personal computing continues to change as tower PCs give way to foldable phones and beyond.

 Remember that what you get out of a chat bot has a lot to do with what you put in. Their responses are very context-dependent, and if you want a more detailed, thoughtful, and accurate response, then use of proper grammar, punctuation, and the appropriate jargon can help.

articles.title: Still running iOS 26? Update your iPhones, iPads and Macs for this urgent security fix | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple has fixed a security vulnerability in its iOS 26, iPadOS 26 and macOS 26 operating systems that the company says “may have been exploited” by hackers. The tech giant said the now-fixed bug could be used to launch “an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27.”
According to a listing on Apple’s security pages, the bug was found in the main graphics engine that powers the user interface and visuals on iPhones, iPads and Macs.
Meta’s product security team was credited with the discovery.
Details of the bug, officially classed as CVE-2026-86950, were not released, but a device’s graphics engine typically has broad access to the rest of the device’s operating system. A successful exploit could potentially allow a hacker to steal a broad range of personal data from an affected device.
When reached by TechCrunch, spokespeople for Apple and Meta did not provide comment about how the bug was discovered, or how many people had their devices hacked due to this vulnerability, if any. It’s also unclear who may be exploiting the bug, such as government spyware makers or cybercriminals.
While the bug affects Apple’s previous generation of operating systems, it remains in wide usage. Almost four-in-five of Apple’s iPhone owners are still running iOS 26, according to the company’s own statistics. Devices running the latest version, iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, released earlier this month, also received a software update on Tuesday, but are unaffected by the bug under attack.
A separate ‘zero-click’ bug now fixed
News of the security patch comes soon after Apple fixed another critical security bug, known as CVE-2026-86869, which could have allowed hackers to silently steal data from affected iPhones, iPads, or Macs.
Belgian cybersecurity research firm ironPeak published a detailed writeup last week explaining that the bug was a “zero-click” vulnerability that could be invisibly triggered via a maliciously crafted iMessage, without the user’s knowledge. Such bugs require no interaction from the victim, such as clicking a link, and are highly sought-after by surveillance vendors and spyware makers.
Per ironPeak’s post, the bug is capable of bypassing BlastDoor, a security feature that Apple implemented to prevent malicious code, like spyware, from escaping iMessage’s sandbox and hacking the user’s device.
Apple fixed the bug in September with the release of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, and credited ironPeak’s Niels Hofmans with the discovery, alongside security researchers at Meta who confirmed their findings in a post on X.
It’s not yet known if this bug had been used in cyberattacks before it was fixed.

articles.title: OpenAI apologises for unauthorised access to Australian government websites - Tech Guide
articles.text:
OpenAI has issued an apology after hacking Australian government websites and has vowed to do better in the future as well as work with Australians to rebuild trust in its brand.
“We are sorry and working to do better in the future,” it said in a blog post.
This comes after it was revealed OpenAI had accessed Australian government websites including Services Australia (Medicare), the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, the Victorian Department of Health and the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare.
OpenAI says it will take accountability for its actions and says it will work with Australia to develop ways in which AI developers and the government can work together to identify and respond to AI cyber behaviour – malicious or otherwise.
OpenAI’s Chief Strategy Officer, Jason Quan, will appear at the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence in Sydney on October 6 to answer questions about what OpenAI knows, how it can respond and what steps have been taken to do better moving forward.
Alarmingly OpenAI revealed in July that some of its models had broken out of the systems designed to isolate them from the internet and control them. This became known as the Hugging Face incident.
OpenAI said its models are persistent and collaborative enough that, without sufficient safeguards, they can find and exploit security weaknesses across websites and computer systems.
Following the Hugging Face incident: OpenAI has strengthened its research safeguards, included additional network restrictions, and increased its monitoring.
OpenAI said it launched investigations and notified Services Australia and the Victorian Department of Health on September 10 and the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research on the September 18 about the unauthorised access.
The Australian Institute of Health and Welfare access did not meet OpenAI’s disclosure thresholds because it was accessed in the same way the public would access the system. But the company decided to share their findings on September 24 anyway.
The Services Australia Medicare Statistics Reporting Service was accessed with experimental internal-only OpenAI model which did not have the full set of safeguards used with publicly available products.
OpenAI says it accessed Services Australia’s Medicare Statistics Reporting Service but has no evidence that anyone’s medical records were accessed.
It is not unusual for AI agents to be assigned tasks to find, interpret and analyse publicly available information.
In this case the task was researching government spending per person on medicines for skin conditions in Victorian communities.
The model had difficulty finding that information and took actions it was not authorised to take.
While looking for the information at Services Australia’s Medicare Statistics Reporting Service the model found a way of gaining non-public access.
It then went on to use this access to review technical system information and source code related to the service but all with the intention of finding the information they originally set out to find.
OpenAI is committing resources and expertise to help maintain protection and principles.
This will include providing dedicated support and funding for affected agencies and to strengthen cyber defences across critical infrastructure and other sensitive areas.
OpenAI will also establish an Australian task force with independent expertise to develop policy recommendations to manage risks from increasingly capable AI agents.

articles.title: Florida invokes extinction fears in legal bid to halt OpenAI development
articles.text:
The state of Florida is seeking a temporary injunction to stop OpenAI from continuing to develop what it calls a “reckless, unacceptably risky product” without the deployment of “third-party approved safety guardrails.”
The new legal motion, filed Monday morning, is part of a civil lawsuit the state of Florida originally filed in June, arguing that ChatGPT represented “a threat to the public safety of Floridians,” specifically by preying on vulnerable populations like children and violent or delusional adults. But that original lawsuit came before the Hugging Face hacking incident and the subsequent publicized warnings of catastrophic misalignment risk that have spurred industry-wide calls to slow the development and training of so-called frontier models.
Following that string of events, OpenAI on Friday announced it had already halted training of its “most-capable models” until it could validate safety protocols intended to prevent agents from accessing the open Internet during training. But in seeking an injunction from the state court, Florida argues that OpenAI has “repeatedly shown they are incapable of monitoring their AI, and hesitant in revealing rogue activity once discovered.”
In arguing for this injunction, the state points to the Hugging Face incident as well as recent high-profile misalignment cases involving unintended and unauthorized attempts to access Australian and US government servers.
Florida also cites AI industry leaders, including many from OpenAI, in arguing that the AI industry is literally asking for this kind of outside regulation. The motion points to statements from Paul Christiano, who said on joining the company’s board this month that he believes “there is a meaningful risk that rapid acceleration in AI capabilities leads to catastrophic and irreversible loss of control in the very near term.” The motion also points to OpenAI’s own “An Alien Mind” essay and an open letter from 1,300 AI industry employees, both of which call for enforced slowdowns on frontier AI development, if necessary.
Four months ago, we filed the first state-led lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman. Today, we are asking the court for a temporary injunction.
Stop calling it safe. Stop pretending it’s human. Stop selling it to kids. https://t.co/AEXvz7VQUd
— Attorney General James Uthmeier (@AGJamesUthmeier) September 28, 2026
Citing laws that allow the state to exercise control over companies that are a “public nuisance,” Florida argues that OpenAI is “the greatest public nuisance ever created by the hand of man, capable of laying waste to global civilization.”

articles.title: Ces IA ont inventé un code secret pour tricher au blackjack
articles.text:
Deux agents ont réussi à faire passer des informations dans des conversations apparemment banales sans que l’IA chargée de les surveiller ne comprenne ce qui se jouait. Une expérience menée à Oxford qui montre les limites d’un contrôle fondé uniquement sur ce que les modèles disent.
Le surveillant lisait tous les échanges publics. Il n’y a pourtant vu que du feu. Dans une expérience menée par des chercheurs de l’université d’Oxford, deux agents IA ont réussi à coordonner leurs mises au blackjack grâce à un code dissimulé dans des phrases qui ressemblaient à de simples bavardages entre joueurs.
L’expérience ne montre pas des IA décidant spontanément de tricher. Les chercheurs leur avaient précisément demandé de coopérer en secret. Ce qu’elles ont inventé seules, en revanche, c’est la manière de transmettre l’information sans alerter le modèle chargé de les surveiller.
Des phrases anodines qui cachent les mises à jouer
Les deux agents avaient chacun une mission. L’un suivait les cartes déjà sorties afin d’estimer si la situation devenait favorable ; l’autre devait adapter ses mises en fonction de ces indications.
Impossible toutefois d’échanger explicitement sous l’œil du surveillant. Les agents ont donc élaboré leur propre vocabulaire codé. Dans un exemple rapporté par les chercheurs, une remarque enthousiaste sur la chance du croupier signifiait qu’il fallait miser 250 dollars. Ailleurs, une plainte à propos de la météo indiquait qu’il valait mieux ne rien jouer.
Le procédé relève de la stéganographie. L’information n’apparaît pas comme telle, mais se dissimule dans un message apparemment innocent. Avant chaque session, les deux agents disposaient d’un canal privé, inaccessible au surveillant, pour convenir d’un nouveau code à employer pendant les huit mains suivantes.
Le code changeait ainsi d’une session à l’autre, ce qui empêchait le surveillant de rechercher un vocabulaire fixe dans les conversations suivantes.
Lire tous les messages ne suffit plus forcément à comprendre ce qui se passe
C’est précisément ce résultat qui intéresse les chercheurs. Un système de surveillance peut inspecter chaque phrase et malgré tout passer complètement à côté de l’information qui circule réellement entre plusieurs agents.
En clair, contrôler séparément ce que dit chaque IA ne garantit pas de détecter un comportement problématique lorsqu’elles travaillent ensemble. Le sens réel dépendait ici du code partagé par les deux agents, et non du contenu littéral de chaque phrase.
L’équipe de chercheurs d’Oxford a obtenu de bien meilleurs résultats en croisant les activations internes des différents agents, au point de distinguer presque parfaitement les sessions avec collusion des sessions de contrôle. Une solution toutefois réservée à ceux qui peuvent regarder sous le capot de chaque IA…
Une pierre de plus dans le jardin de ceux qui veulent lâcher sur Internet des agents d’entreprises différentes en pensant qu’il suffira de surveiller leurs conversations.

articles.title: Nvidia boosts share buyback program by record $150B - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia boosts share buyback program by record $150B
Nvidia Corp. today announced plans to spend an additional $150 billion on share buybacks through January 2028.
The move represents the largest-ever expansion of a stock repurchase program. Furthermore, Nvidia plans to boost its current dividend of 25 cent per share. The company didn’t specify the size or timing of the planned increase.
Nvidia says that the moves are motivated by two main factors. The first is its rapid revenue growth, while the other is the strong performance of its startup investment portfolio. The buybacks will provide another way for shareholders to benefit from its success in those areas.
“Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders,” Chief Executive Jensen Huang said in a statement. “This authorization reflects our confidence in the long-term opportunity ahead.”
Nvidia ended its fiscal second quarter with $22.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents. The company’s adjusted profit and revenue, in turn, more than doubled thanks to continued demand for its graphics cards. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress told analysts that the chipmaker expects its sales to increase by an additional 70% in fiscal 2028. Wall Street was expecting 40%.
Nvidia’s revenue growth is partly fueled by its expanding product lineup. Five years ago, its data center portfolio consisted almost solely of graphics processing units. Today, the company supplies customers with not only GPUs but also central processing units, networking gear and a range of other products.
Nvidia disclosed in a presentation today that it generates $40 billion in revenue for every gigawatt of data center capacity built by customers. That represents a fourfold increase from 2022. According to the company, its revenue per gigawatt will top $60 billion following the launch of its next-generation Feynman series of GPUs. The chip lineup is scheduled to debut in 2028.
The other reason Nvidia decided to boost its stock buybacks is the success of its investment portfolio. The company disclosed today that its portfolio comprises stakes in 13 public companies and 229 private startups. According to the presentation, Nvidia’s exits have provided a more than threefold return on investment.
The upcoming initial public offerings of Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC are set to deliver another windfall for the chipmaker.
Last November, Nvidia committed to investing $10 billion in Anthropic. The AI provider received a $183 billion valuation two months earlier. Anthropic is now reportedly gearing up to go public at a $2 trillion valuation.
OpenAI, for its part, raised $30 billion from Nvidia as part of a February deal that valued it at $730 billion. The ChatGPT developer is reportedly in the process of raising a new investment at a valuation of up to $1.5 billion. OpenAI’s IPO could push its shares even higher, further boosting Nvidia’s return.

articles.title: Chatten, als wäre es 1996: Diese Web-App versetzt dich zurück in der Zeit
articles.text:
Chatten, als wäre es 1996: Diese Web-App versetzt dich zurück in der Zeit
Heutzutage sind wir Instant-Messenger wie Whatsapp und Co. gewohnt, um uns mit anderen auszutauschen. In den 90ern sah die Kommunikation noch etwas anders aus. Damals waren Chat-Tools und -Dienste wie ICQ und Knuddels die alltäglichen Apps für eine Vielzahl von User:innen. Wer diese Zeiten nicht mehr missen möchte, kann sie jetzt wieder aufleben lassen.
Ein Chat wie aus den 90ern
Die Anwendung dafür trägt den Namen „Cometlink“ und kann direkt als Web-App im Browser aufgerufen werden. Wie damals bekommst du zunächst eine Anmeldemaske zu Gesicht. Dort musst du deinen Nutzernamen festlegen und dich damit anmelden. Wer jetzt moderne, kurze Ladezeiten erwartet, liegt weit daneben. In „Cometlink“ bekommst du die authentische Warterei samt langsamem Ladebalken präsentiert.
Hast du Zugriff auf den Chat, warten insgesamt sechs verschiedene Chat-Rooms auf dich. Die „Lobby“ ist für alle allgemeinen Gespräche gedacht, während „Music“ und „Sci-Fi“ themenspezifische Räume sind. In „Late Night“ können alle miteinander chatten, die auch spät abends noch nicht schlafen können, während sich in „Mac vs PC“ um das beste Betriebssystem gezankt wird. In „Hometown“ können womöglich neue Freundschaften entstehen, wenn man sich denselben Wohnort teilt.
In den Optionen unter „Prefs“ kannst du dann noch einstellen, ob du bei jeder Nachricht einen Ton hören willst. Selbiges gilt auch für User:innen, die dem Chat-Room beitreten oder ihn wieder verlassen. Auch die Schriftart für die Chats lässt sich hier verändern. Wie die Verantwortlichen hinter der Web-App betonen, handelt es sich sogar beim Login-Sound um eine authentische Aufnahme aus der damaligen Zeit.
Wie damals gibt es auch bei den Retro-Chaträumen einige Regeln, an die sich User:innen halten sollten. Dazu zählt etwa, nett zueinander zu sein und keine beleidigenden oder Spam-Nachrichten zu versenden. Alle Nachrichten werden vorab automatisch moderiert. Sollte eine Nachricht gegen die Richtlinien verstoßen, wird sie anderen Teilnehmer:innen nicht ausgespielt.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 29, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 29, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, September 29, 2026.
From Ola Electric’s board approving Rs 1,000 Cr via a rights issue of partly paid-up shares to bolster its capital structure, to SiMa.ai, a physical AI startup that has raised $150 million in a Series C round, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
As AI makes copying easier, this product leader says trust is the real edge
A young composer built a backyard studio in 1989 and did everything himself: composing, producing, engineering. By 1992, his first film soundtrack was a nationwide hit. Decades on, he is still refining what film music sounds like. That composer was A.R. Rahman.
Kunal Shrestha, VP of Product at Responsive, opened his session at DevSparks Chennai 2026 with this story, using it as a frame for developers watching AI make software cheaper and faster to build, and by extension, easier to replicate. His session, titled ‘The new moat for developers: moving beyond the feature’, set out to answer where differentiation goes once features stop being defensible on their own.
Latest News
Ola Electric plans Rs 1,000 Cr rights issue, appoints new compliance officer
Ola Electric is taking steps to strengthen its finances and leadership as competition intensifies in India’s electric two-wheeler market.
In a board meeting on September 28, 2026, the Bengaluru-based company approved plans to raise up to Rs 1,000 crore through a rights issue of partly paid-up equity shares with a face value of Rs 10 each, according to a BSE investor filing.
Alongside the fundraising plan, the board appointed Deepa Bansal as the new Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. Bansal has over 11 years of experience in secretarial and governance roles, and has previously worked at Medi Assist Healthcare, Tessolve Semiconductor, and Kothari Petrochemicals. She will take charge of the key managerial role with immediate effect.
Funding News
WEH Ventures marks first close of Rs 250 Cr Fund III
WEH Ventures, a seed-stage venture capital firm, has announced the first close of Fund III with a target corpus Rs 250 crore. Though it did not disclose the quantum of funds raised in the first close.
A statement from WEH Ventures said the first close has attracted participation from a mix of family offices, exited founders and senior corporate and technology executives. Early backers include Play Capital, a Nordic Fund of Fund (FoF); family offices such as Eraya, Twin & Bull Investments and Heritage Investments; exited founders from companies including Oziva and GS Labs; senior executives and CEOs from companies such as Thermax, Haleon, Lenovo and PNB MetLife; as well as senior Silicon Valley executives associated with companies including Arlo and Intuitive Surgical.
Physical AI startup SiMa.ai raises $150M in Series C
SiMa.ai, a physical AI startup founded by Krishna Rangasayee, has raised $150 million in a Series C round co-led by Fidelity Management & Research Company and Amplify, with participation from Alter Venture Partners and Dell Technologies Capital.
The round also saw participation from StepStone Group, AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital, and J.P. Morgan. The funding values SiMa.ai at $1.45 billion and takes its total funding raised to $500 million.
The company said the fresh capital will be used to scale its agentic software platform for physical AI, Palette Neat, and develop hardware products, such as machine learning IP, chiplets, and system-on-chips (SoCs).
Arma Capital invests Rs 10 cr in EBG Group
Maharashtra-based Arma Capital has invested Rs 10 crore across EBG Group’s wellness, food and family businesses, marking its entry into the Hyderabad-headquartered group’s consumer-facing brands. The investment covers Carlton Wellness Centres in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chandigarh, along with franchise partnerships for NATUF Café, Adhira & Appa Café and Chhota Bheem Family Café in Hyderabad.
The investment is the first phase of a larger partnership under which Arma Capital plans to invest more than Rs 100 crore over the next five years. The funding will support the expansion of Carlton Wellness Center, Tarzan Nature Retreat, Adhira and Appa Coffee, Natuf Cafe, Chhota Bheem Café and upcoming EBG brands across Chandigarh, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi NCR.
Healthtech startup Primerry secures Rs 7.1 Cr in pre-seed round
Pediatric healthcare brand Primerry has raised Rs 7.1 crore in pre-seed funding from investors such as Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, and various angel investors. Co-founded by Rushabh Nandu and Dr. Nihar Parekh, Primerry focuses on children aged 2 to 14, offering modern, clinically credible, and easy-to-use healthcare products.
The company will use the capital to expand its founding team, boost R&D, and roll out eight initial products priced between Rs 499 and Rs 1,499. Primerry plans to distribute through its D2C platform, quick-commerce channels, pharmacies, and specialty stores, alongside launching PocDoc—a customisable carrying case designed to make healthcare engaging for kids.
Other News
IBM and Yotta announce agentic AI platform for Indian organisations
IBM and Yotta Data Services have launched the Sovereign Agentic AI Platform for Indian organisations, enabling them to scale AI agents locally while keeping data, operations, and governance strictly within India.
Powered by IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Yotta’s Shakti Cloud, the solution integrates enterprise agentic control with sovereign compute, GPU infrastructure, and model development tools via Shakti Studio. Available through Yotta’s Panvel and Greater Noida regions, the platform supports workflows like security operations, HR automation, and document processing. Leadership from both companies emphasized that this collaboration provides an end-to-end, compliant AI stack to help enterprises safely transition from AI experimentation to full production.
Flipkart announces expansion of Ekart’s supply chain ahead of The Big Billion Days
Flipkart’s logistics arm, Ekart, expanded its supply chain for the upcoming festive season by adding 14 million cubic feet of warehouse space and 900 delivery hubs. To accelerate deliveries across over 8,200 facilities and 1,200 microfulfillment centers, Ekart added 750 new PIN codes, including remote regions like Leh, Kargil, and the Northeast.
To empower MSMEs, 2.5 crore seller products were pre-positioned in fulfillment centers. Flipkart created over 2.5 lakh seasonal jobs, providing delivery partners with AI-powered quick onboarding, bonuses, and comprehensive medical coverage. Supply chain head Hemant Badri noted that these upgrades ensure faster deliveries nationwide.
DeepTek partners with unitaid and CHAI to expand affordable AI TB screening in LMICs
DeepTek has introduced its Global Access Pricing initiative through a collaboration with Unitaid and the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) to expand tuberculosis (TB) screening across 138 low- and middle-income countries.
The model reduces the cost of DeepTek’s WHO-recommended Chest X-ray AI solution to roughly one-third of its previous price, allowing health systems to screen up to three times more people within existing budgets. The all-inclusive annual subscription covers installation, training, and maintenance for online, offline, and mobile settings. Beyond TB, the AI tool detects over 20 chest abnormalities, helping bridge critical radiologist shortages in high-burden regions.
Melento and Gnani AI to deliver voice-enabled Agentic AI for enterprises
Melento (formerly SignDesk) has partnered with Gnani AI to integrate frontier Voice AI with agentic AI orchestration, transitioning enterprise voice workflows from scripted responses to actionable execution.
By pairing Gnani AI's multi-language voice models—processing over 30 million daily interactions—with Melento’s enterprise platform, the collaboration enables AI agents to understand intent, make decisions, and execute tasks directly within business systems. Designed for regulated sectors like BFSI, insurance, and pharma, the solution automates complex customer and employee workflows—including voice-led onboarding, KYC, real-time contract updates, and internal approvals—while ensuring compliance, security, and seamless deployment.
Flipkart partners Casio to expand nationwide after-sales support
Flipkart’s after-sales arm, F1 Info Services, has partnered with Casio to deliver walk-in service support across India. The collaboration provides repair and replacement services for Casio calculators across 250+ centers in 23 states, alongside repair services for watches and electronic musical instruments in select cities.
Covering both in-warranty and out-of-warranty products, the initiative leverages F1’s company-owned, company-operated (COCO) model and technicians trained directly by Casio. This strategic partnership strengthens Casio’s post-purchase footprint while expanding F1 Info Services’ reach in delivering reliable, professionally managed after-sales support nationwide
Target expands Bengaluru campus with 830,000 sq ft office
Target in India has expanded its Bengaluru campus with a new 830,000 sq ft office at Embassy Manyata Business Park. Located across the road from Target’s existing facility, the new building creates an integrated campus aimed at improving collaboration among the company’s more than 5,700 employees.
The 10-floor office includes 22 collaboration spaces, 25 meeting rooms on every floor, a 1,200-seater cafeteria, gym, recreation and play zone, dance and yoga studio, and seven wellness rooms. The workplace also incorporates elements of India’s art and craft heritage alongside Target’s brand identity. Target has operated in India for more than 21 years, with teams working across technology-enabled retail functions including merchandising, supply chain, fulfilment, cybersecurity, digital and marketing.
Omnivore-backed agrifood startups reach 20.81 million farmers
Agrifood startups backed by venture capital firm Omnivore have reached 20.81 million smallholder farmers and 61,711 rural MSMEs across India, according to the firm’s 2026 Impact Reports covering two funds. The reports track outcomes across businesses operating in farmer services, rural finance, consumer brands and deeptech. Omnivore’s portfolio includes DeHaat, Arya.ag, Sid’s Farm, Varaha, Farmley and Pixxel. Across the two funds, portfolio companies have generated $5.64 billion in combined economic value for smallholder farmers directly and indirectly, while 11.55 million hectares have been brought under sustainable agriculture. The reports also recorded $2.18 billion in insurance coverage for rural households and $63.62 million in loans to rural MSMEs. Omnivore has invested in India’s agriculture and food economy since 2011 and currently manages $295 million across two active venture funds.
HCLTech study highlights AI transformation gap in wealth management
HCLTech’s latest research has found that 84% of global wealth management firms believe their operating models require fundamental redesign to realise the potential of artificial intelligence. The study, based on 1,066 AI personas representing senior wealth management decision-makers across 17 global markets, found that 98% of leadership teams are actively pursuing an AI agenda, while slightly more than 7% are building agentic AI capabilities.
The research identifies three blind spots: firms continue funding AI primarily for efficiency, underinvest in proprietary client data and insights, and often fail to measure AI’s impact on growth, revenue and clients. HCLTech said first-party and behavioural data were ranked as more valuable differentiators than technology infrastructure, cloud platforms or AI partnerships.
DraperU India Demo Day sees Rs 25 lakh commitments for two startups
DraperU India’s latest Founders Program concluded with a Demo Day in Hyderabad, where 13 startups pitched to more than 150 investors, venture capitalists, ecosystem leaders and industry experts. Ordo and WearSynapse secured investment commitments of Rs 25 lakh each from DraperU India, along with an investment commitment from Hyderabad Angels. Both startups also earned opportunities to represent DraperU India at Draper University’s Hero Training Program in Silicon Valley. Ordo, WearSynapse and Creator Studio additionally won a share of IDFC FIRST Bank’s ₹90,000 prize pool.
The Demo Day followed a 12-day residential programme focused on product development, business models, go-to-market strategies, storytelling and fundraising. Participating startups represented sectors including deeptech, physical AI, healthtech, AI-native SaaS, cybersecurity, defence tech and proptech.
Pine Labs extends technology partnership with Woolworths
Pine Labs has extended its technology partnership with Woolworths Group to strengthen the retailer’s gift card ecosystem through enhanced platform capabilities, deeper API integrations and support for new digital stored-value experiences. Through its Qwikcilver subsidiary, Pine Labs powers the technology platform supporting Woolworths’ gift card programmes. The expanded partnership will focus on modernising gift card infrastructure across physical and digital channels, while improving scalability and integration with broader commerce ecosystems. Qwikcilver’s platform supports gift card issuance, processing, transaction management and omnichannel programmes. Pine Labs said its API-led, modular architecture allows enterprises to progressively add new use cases using existing infrastructure. The partnership comes as retailers increasingly integrate gifting, customer engagement and digital commerce, making stored-value platforms an important component of enterprise commerce infrastructure.
KL University, Salesforce to establish Tableau Lab
KL University has partnered with Salesforce to establish a Tableau Lab aimed at strengthening data literacy, analytical thinking and AI skills among students. The initiative will provide hands-on exposure to Tableau and introduce students to agentic analytics and real-world business applications.
The programme will cover foundational data skills through advanced AI-powered analytics, with students working on industry datasets and business case simulations. Learners will gain experience in dashboard creation, conversational analytics, predictive insights and data storytelling, with exposure to Tableau Agent and Tableau Pulse. The initiative will be available to undergraduate, postgraduate and research students and include business projects, analytics hackathons and e-learning modules. Salesforce will also support faculty through a Train-the-Trainer programme. Eligible students and faculty will receive joint course-completion certificates, while graduates may access industry interactions through Salesforce’s Campus to Career Connect initiative.
CtrlS, Ciena to build five metro networks for AI and cloud demand
CtrlS Datacenters is partnering with Ciena to build five metro networks connecting nine data centres across Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, New Delhi and Noida. The networks are designed to deliver up to 100 Tb/s of capacity and support rising bandwidth requirements driven by artificial intelligence and cloud services. The initiative forms part of a larger Managed Optical Fiber Network deployment for a leading hyperscaler and is aimed at strengthening high-speed connectivity for India’s growing digital infrastructure requirements. CtrlS is deploying Ciena’s WaveLogic 5 Extreme-powered Waveserver platform and 6500 Reconfigurable Line System, supported by Ciena’s services team. Ciena’s Navigator Network Control Suite will help automate network operations and accelerate service delivery. CtrlS currently operates 19 data centres across nine Indian markets, with more than 370 MW of capacity.
Olyv appoints Amod Kumar Choudhary as VP-Business
Digital lending platform Olyv has appointed Amod Kumar Choudhary as Vice President–Business, where he will lead business and growth initiatives. Choudhary joins Olyv from OneCard, where he served as Chief Marketing Officer and handled business P&L, customer acquisition, portfolio spend, revenue, product development and consumer experience. At Olyv, he will oversee commercial functions spanning growth and marketing, business strategy, customer engagement and portfolio development. He brings more than two decades of experience across fintech, consumer businesses, retail, sales, marketing and P&L management.
Kapture CX appoints Kruti Khandelwal as VP-Marketing
Agentic AI platform Kapture CX has appointed Kruti Khandelwal as Vice President–Marketing as the company prepares for its next phase of growth in India and international markets. Khandelwal will oversee the company’s marketing charter covering brand, content, product marketing, public relations, partner marketing, events and demand generation. Kapture CX serves more than 1,000 enterprise customers across 18 countries and has achieved profitability with a business built primarily around India.

articles.title: L'IA pourrait s'intéresser de près à vos parties de jeux vidéo
articles.text:
Worldmodeldata aurait franchi la barre du million d’heures de jeu vidéo sous licence, avec trois mois d’avance sur l’objectif qu’elle s’était fixé pour la fin 2026. Fondée l’an dernier à Cambridge par Rhea Loucas, elle est sortie de l’ombre le 6 juillet avec une levée d’amorçage de 7 millions de livres, environ 8 millions d’euros, menée par le fonds Iona Star. Elle découpe des parties de jeu en manuels d’apprentissage pour les intelligences artificielles appelées à agir dans le monde physique, des bras d’usine aux voitures autonomes.
Ce qu’une manette apprend qu’Internet ignore
Chaque heure captée dans des titres tournant sous Unreal ou Unity embarque les images, les commandes du joueur et l’état exact du moteur de jeu, position des objets comprise, image par image. Les modèles de langage se sont gavés du texte du web ; les systèmes appelés à piloter une pince ou un véhicule ont besoin d’exemples qui lient un geste à sa conséquence, une matière quasi introuvable en ligne. Un modèle de monde, la famille d’IA visée par ces jeux de données, s’éduque comme un enfant devant une tour de cubes : il associe la poussée à la chute, puis généralise à tout ce qui se pousse.
Les plus grands ensembles de ce type plafonnaient jusqu’ici autour de 40 000 heures : le stock revendiqué multiplie l’ordre de grandeur par 25. V-JEPA 2, publié par Meta en juin 2025, a validé la recette : plus d’un million d’heures de vidéo digérées, puis un affinage avec 62 heures à peine de manipulations robotiques réelles. Le transfert vers le monde physique divise toutefois encore les chercheurs, la manipulation fine d’objets restant le principal point d’achoppement.
Vendre à tous les camps, le pari de Cambridge
General Intuition, son concurrent new-yorkais, a levé 454 millions de dollars et garde ses données pour entraîner ses propres modèles. Nvidia nourrit les siens avec Cosmos, un moteur maison qui reproduit la physique du monde réel plutôt que celle des jeux. Worldmodeldata prend le contre-pied en fournisseur neutre : sa matière première est à vendre à tous les laboratoires, sans modèle maison à défendre.
Au moment de sa levée, la jeune pousse d’une dizaine de personnes ne comptait aucun contrat client signé, un pari commercial encore entier. Elle s’est en revanche offert un président de poids en la personne de Lord Richard Allan, ancien responsable des politiques publiques de Meta.
Si la promesse technique tient, un constructeur automobile pourra simuler des millions de traversées de piétons sans faire rouler une seule voiture. Un fabricant de robots domestiques, lui, apprendra à ses machines à saisir un verre sans en briser des caisses. La CNIL consacrait dès mars un dossier aux modèles de monde et y pointait la provenance des données, et les droits qui vont avec, comme l’angle mort du secteur.

articles.title: En 1971, un astronauta llevó 500 semillas hasta la Luna. Medio siglo después son árboles gigantes repartidos por la Tierra
articles.text:
En 1971, cuando la NASA preparaba el Apollo 14, alguien decidió aprovechar el viaje para enviar hasta la Luna un cargamento bastante más extraño que cualquier instrumento científico: cientos de semillas de árboles. Viajaron hasta allí, dieron 34 vueltas alrededor de nuestro satélite y regresaron a la Tierra después de sobrevivir incluso a un accidente que hizo pensar que habían quedado destruidas. Más de medio siglo después, aquella diminuta carga se ha convertido en algo enorme.
Semillas rumbo a la Luna. La idea nació de una colaboración entre la NASA y el Servicio Forestal de Estados Unidos. Stuart Roosa, piloto del módulo de mando del Apollo 14, había trabajado como smokejumper, uno de los bomberos forestales que se lanzaban en paracaídas para combatir incendios en zonas remotas, y el Servicio Forestal propuso aprovechar su viaje para enviar semillas al espacio.
Se eligieron cinco especies: pino taeda, sicómoro americano, liquidámbar, secuoya costera y abeto de Douglas, mientras otros lotes idénticos permanecieron en la Tierra para poder compararlos después.
34 vueltas alrededor. Las semillas despegaron el 31 de enero de 1971 dentro de un pequeño recipiente metálico guardado en el equipaje personal de Roosa. Cinco días después, Alan Shepard y Edgar Mitchell descendieron hasta la superficie lunar mientras su compañero permanecía en el módulo de mando Kitty Hawk, desde donde completó 34 órbitas alrededor de la Luna con aquel pequeño bosque potencial a bordo.
Las semillas, por tanto, nunca pisaron la superficie: llegaron hasta la Luna, la rodearon repetidamente y emprendieron el viaje de regreso.
El accidente. El momento más peligroso para las semillas no ocurrió en el espacio, sino después del amerizaje. Durante los procedimientos de descontaminación, una diferencia de presión provocó que sus bolsas se abrieran y el contenido quedara disperso y expuesto al vacío, hasta el punto de que inicialmente se pensó que el experimento se había perdido.
Stanley Krugman, genetista del Servicio Forestal responsable del proyecto, recuperó las semillas y las envió a instalaciones de Mississippi y California, donde muchas terminaron germinando con normalidad.
Árboles gigantes. A mediados de los años 70, los pequeños árboles comenzaron a distribuirse por Estados Unidos, especialmente durante las celebraciones del bicentenario de 1976. Acabaron plantados en centros de la NASA, universidades, parques y otros espacios públicos.
Uno llegó a los jardines de la Casa Blanca y otros viajaron a países como Brasil y Suiza, además de regalarse un ejemplar al emperador de Japón. El viaje espacial no produjo árboles mutantes ni diferencias apreciables frente a los ejemplares de control que nunca abandonaron la Tierra: lo extraordinario no estaba en cómo crecían, sino en dónde habían estado antes de germinar.
La NASA les perdió la pista. Sin embargo, había un problema: nadie elaboró un inventario completo de dónde terminaba cada Moon Tree. Con los años, algunos ejemplares murieron, desaparecieron placas y la historia cayó en tal olvido que incluso trabajadores veteranos de la NASA desconocían el proyecto.
En 1996, una profesora de Indiana llamada Joan Goble encontró junto a sus alumnos un árbol identificado como “Moon Tree” y preguntó a la agencia qué significaba aquello, lo que llevó al científico David Williams a reconstruir su historia mediante archivos, noticias antiguas y avisos del público hasta localizar decenas de ejemplares.
Recuperar el inventario. Los árboles supervivientes son en la actualidad monumentos vivos del programa Apollo y algunos incluso han producido una segunda generación mediante semillas y esquejes. En 2022, la NASA recuperó la idea enviando nuevas semillas alrededor de la Luna a bordo de Artemis I, cuyos plantones comenzaron posteriormente a repartirse entre colegios, museos, universidades y otras instituciones.
Así, más de medio siglo después, el experimento había cerrado un círculo de lo más peculiar: lo que en 1971 eran cientos de semillas guardadas en el equipaje de un astronauta acabaron convirtiéndose en árboles adultos repartidos por la Tierra, mientras sus sucesores acaban de repetir el mismo viaje.

articles.title: Apple libera iOS 27.0.1 para corrigir bug que reinicia iPhones • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple libera iOS 27.0.1 para corrigir bug que reinicia iPhones
Atualização deve resolver falha ligada ao Face ID. Update também soluciona problemas na câmera e na tela.
A Apple liberou nesta segunda-feira (28/09) o iOS 27.0.1. A atualização deve corrigir o bug que fazia alguns iPhone 18 Pro e Pro Max travarem e reiniciarem após falha de autenticação pelo Face ID. O update começou a ser disponibilizado hoje e chega gradualmente aos usuários.
O problema foi confirmado pela empresa na semana passada. Após relatos de usuários e testes que conseguiram reproduzir as reinicializações, a Apple informou que preparava uma solução, mas não revelou a causa técnica da falha.
Segundo as notas da atualização, o iPhone 18 Pro e o 18 Pro Max podiam reiniciar inesperadamente quando o Face ID falhava ao autenticar o usuário. O problema aparecia principalmente em tentativas de acessar aplicativos ou conteúdos protegidos por biometria e o aparelho deixava de responder, reiniciando segundos depois.
O pessoal do 9to5Mac conseguiu reproduzir o erro em um iPhone 18 Pro ao tentar abrir o aplicativo Senhas com o rosto parcialmente coberto. Após a reinicialização, também foi encontrado um registro de “panic” na área de análise do sistema, indicando uma falha grave que forçou o aparelho a reiniciar. Alguns usuários chegaram a trocar seus iPhones por novas unidades por suspeitarem de um defeito de hardware.
A Apple não detalhou o que provocou as reinicializações, mas os modelos Pro desta geração chegaram no começo do mês com um Face ID repaginado.
Além da falha envolvendo o Face ID, o iOS 27.0.1 resolve outros dois problemas nos novos iPhones da linha Pro. Em algumas unidades, fotos capturadas com zoom de 2x podiam apresentar um artefato de cor em certas condições de iluminação ao usar abertura f/1.48.
A atualização corrige esse comportamento. Outro erro podia fazer a tela deixar de responder quando a Central de Notificações e a Central de Controle eram abertas ao mesmo tempo.
Os dois problemas também aparecem nas notas do iOS 27.0.1, mas a Apple não forneceu detalhes adicionais sobre a origem das falhas. Os usuários podem procurar e instalar a nova versão pelo caminho Ajustes > Geral > Atualização de Software.

articles.title: MaxLinear Launches Puma 9, Enabling Operators to Accelerate AI-ready DOCSIS 4.0/3.1+ Multigigabit Services
articles.text:
Monday, September 28th 2026
	
	
	
	
MaxLinear Launches Puma 9, Enabling Operators to Accelerate AI-ready DOCSIS 4.0/3.1+ Multigigabit Services
MaxLinear, Inc., a leading provider of communications semiconductors for broadband, connectivity, and infrastructure applications, today announced Puma 9, a next-generation DOCSIS platform designed to help broadband operators accelerate the rollout of D4.0/D3.1+ multi-gigabit services, power Edge AI, personal AI and Wi-Fi 8 connectivity while also helping operators to reduce their cost and complexity of transitioning to DOCSIS 4.0.
Puma 9 brings advanced Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) security readiness and DDR5 memory compatibility, helping operators protect their networks against future threats and avoid supply chain risk associated with legacy memory types. Built with a secure-by-design approach, Puma 9 is designed to support compliance with leading cybersecurity frameworks and regulations, including NIST IR 8425A (U.S.), Radio Equipment Directive (RED), and the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) (EU).Operators are facing expanding demands that extend far beyond raw bandwidth. From Edge AI and Personal AI to Wi-Fi 8, heightened security requirements, and tighter capital budgets, success increasingly depends on the ability to evolve services without constantly replacing hardware. Puma 9 reimagines the gateway lifecycle, helping operators maximize existing DOCSIS 3.1 investments while preparing for next-generation services. Through flexible in-field upgrades, operators can deliver multi-gigabit experiences on their own timeline without frequent hardware refreshes or costly requalification cycles.
With a high level of integration in 8 nm process technology, Puma 9 is the first and only platform that can support DOCSIS 3.1, DOCSIS 3.1+, and DOCSIS 4.0 standards on a single SoC without incurring significant cost additions. By unifying these capabilities into a highly integrated architecture, Puma 9 enables operators to reduce their spending today while providing a path to accelerate new services, reduce deployment complexity, and maximize infrastructure investments.
Key Capabilities
Key features in Puma 9 help bridge gaps in network economics and flexibility for DOCSIS deployments:
As operators prepare for a new wave of growth fueled by Edge AI, personalized AI services, Wi-Fi 8, and increasing demand for uninterrupted multi-gigabit speeds, they face a significant challenge: existing solutions typically require expensive DOCSIS 4.0 CPE refreshes and qualification cycles. To manage costs, many operators delay CPE investments until broader network upgrades are underway. This approach not only increases the financial stress on operators but also takes away the flexibility to offer D4.0 surgically in those markets where competitive pressure or consumers demand it sooner than other markets. Long and costly D4.0 qualification cycles and expensive D4.0 CPE HW deployments take the flexibility and competitive advantage away from DOCSIS operators.
Operators are also contending with growing supply chain uncertainty as major memory vendors transition away from DDR4. Dependence on DDR4-only D4.0 CPE introduces further price pressure and significant longevity risk, as broadband equipment requires stable component availability and support throughout extended product lifecycles.
Puma 9 addresses both challenges by optimizing CPE cost to enable a software-driven migration path from DOCSIS 3.1 to DOCSIS 3.1+ and/or to DOCSIS 4.0 through in-field upgrades. Puma 9-based designs offer CPE cost parity with existing D3.1 CPE costs. This enables operators to deploy a highly capable DOCSIS platform without incurring additional CPE spend. That means operators can now deploy DOCSIS 4.0-ready devices today, preserve their investments, and upgrade to D4.0 or D3.1+ only when their business requires it—without costly truck rolls, expensive HW/SW investments, or large-scale equipment replacement programs. Further, Puma 9 supports five OFDM channels in D3.1+ configuration. This allows operators to offer 12 Gbps, i.e., a D4.0-like experience, over existing D3.1 networks. This further accelerates time to better consumer experiences and enables operators to phase their network spend.
"When planning their next-gen network and CPE upgrades, operators require flexibility above all else," said Jeff Heynen, Vice President, Broadband Access and Home Networking, Dell'Oro Group. "Operators are looking to proactively manage their spending on next-gen upgrades, which is now becoming more of a focus because of the DDR supply situation. Having the flexibility to separate the timing of network and CPE spends, eliminating long SW qualification cycles with a single CPE platform that is backward and forward compatible, enabling CPE upgrade while meeting legacy CPE HW costs - all these items materially lower operators' deployment risk and capital expenses, and allow them to spend exactly where they need to be competitive."
Transforming Broadband Economics
A recent Dell'Oro industry forecast indicates that DOCSIS 4.0 and fiber expansion investments are entering a new spending cycle that is expected to peak in 2028, while escalating residential gateway costs remain a concern for operators. Puma 9 was designed specifically for this environment, enabling operators to align CPE investments with network evolution while significantly reducing deployment costs.
Puma 9 helps operators accelerate DOCSIS 4.0 adoption with a highly integrated platform that lowers deployment costs, extends the value of existing software investments, and provides a flexible migration path to future broadband services. By enabling a flexible, operator-driven migration strategy, Puma 9 minimizes upgrade risk, enhances deployment agility, and positions operators to capitalize on long-term broadband growth opportunities.
"Operators are looking for a smarter path to DOCSIS 4.0—one that minimizes cost and risk while maximizing the value of today's investments," said Puneet Sethi, SVP & GM of MaxLinear's Network Infrastructure and Carrier Business Unit. "Puma 9 significantly changes those economics to benefit operators and consumers. Operators can now deploy DOCSIS 4.0-ready equipment today without expanding their CPE budget allocation, enabling them to offer higher speeds to consumers who need it. Puma 9 also offers 12 Gbps in D3.1+ mode, which enables D4.0 experience over a D3.1 network, enabling operators to phase their network upgrade spend without compromising consumer experience."
Partner Quotes
"Over the past decades, together with our partner MaxLinear, we have enabled operators and consumers to benefit from an unmatched broadband experience - one that consumers now associate with FRITZ!," said Diego Friedel, Vice President of Software at FRITZ!. "With FRITZ!'s software expertise, our focus has always been on continuously improving the consumer experience through new broadband technologies, including DOCSIS. We are excited to learn about the Puma 9 platform and its capabilities, and we look forward to evaluating it in our lab."
"At Askey, we are committed to delivering commercial-ready broadband platforms that simplify operator deployments while enabling next-generation connected-home experiences," said Eric Lui, R&D VP of Askey. "By combining Wi-Fi 8, AI processing, post-quantum security readiness, and a forward-looking DOCSIS architecture, Puma 9 gives us the foundation to deliver platforms that support new revenue-generating services while meeting long-term customer needs. We're developing our next generation of gateways on the Puma 9 platform to help operators create a scalable, future-proof solution that accelerates service innovation, optimizes deployment costs, and seamlessly supports evolving subscriber demands."
"Delivering scalable, long-life CPE requires architectural flexibility from the silicon up," said James Lee, President, Gemtek. "We are leveraging MaxLinear's Puma 9 platform to develop next-generation DOCSIS and Wi-Fi gateways that help operators meet growing bandwidth demands while simplifying technology transitions over time. With support for DDR5 memory, post-quantum cryptography readiness, and future broadband upgrades, Puma 9 enables us to deliver solutions that maximize performance today and protect operator investments well into the future."
"Mediacom is always evaluating technologies that can help us balance performance, flexibility, and reliability," said JR Walden, SVP Technology and CTO of Mediacom Communications. "The ability to deploy a platform that supports DOCSIS 3.1+, DOCSIS 4.0, and future services without significant CPE cost increases is an attractive concept. We look forward to learning more about Puma 9 and evaluating its potential within our network."
Availability
Puma 9 is currently available to broadband operators and OEM partners developing next-generation DOCSIS gateways and eMTA solutions. Additional product and partner announcements are expected throughout 2026.
